chapters.title: Chapter 901: The Apocalypse (5)
paragraphs: "Krez, come here," Vexthra called out.
The undying cockroach in the legion stepped forward with a smile on his face.
"You see that lady surrounded by red flames? Go and protect her secretly," Vexthra pointed at Lady Liora.
Krez, who was already hungry to get into the battle, moved, and soon, he was on the battlefield, fighting at an acceptable distance from Lady Liora.
He wasn’t too close to draw suspicion, and he certainly wasn’t too far to be unable to intervene if Lady Liora needed help.
Unity, who also wanted to enter the battle, walked toward Vexthra and held her hand. "Big sister, why did you ask Krez to go protect her, and don’t you think he alone is not enough to protect her?"
Vexthra just laughed, knowing what Unity was aiming at. "Krez is enough. I only asked him to go there just in case something unexpected happens. I even doubt she will require his help.
"As for your first question, this lady is a Grand Disciple of a Celestial who once helped me when I seriously needed it."
"Wow." The ladies exclaimed and looked toward Lady Liora. Seeing the brown haired beauty fighting, their interest was piqued.
"Who is this Celestial?" Selene asked, moving closer to Vexthra.
"I don’t know her name. However, her disciple is a powerful Supreme called Purple Flame Lady." Vexthra pointed at the flame runes on Lady Liora’s arm and forehead.

"Those runes on her body are flame runes, each connected to a different aspect of her body and some external aspects. Whenever she kills someone, the soul power of the deceased will be absorbed by the flame runes on her body.
"These flame runes are from a technique called ’Flame God’s Mercy’. I don’t know how strong it is; however, this Celestial I know used just one to kill a Celestial beast in one strike."
"Wow." Everyone who heard what Vexthra said became shocked for a moment.
"How can such a powerful technique find its way to a medium world?" Ankaara, the ice elemental, who had some fair knowledge of how devastating Celestial battles can be, asked.
Killing a Celestial beast with just one flame rune was something she never expected anyone in a medium world to have. Yet, looking at Lady Liora, she counted six of such runes on her body.
"This lady isn’t from a medium world. She is much stronger than a Core Formation expert. If she were to free herself, I am sure she would even surpass most of you.
I can sense a rather strong aura of death on her, so I am inclined to believe she is from a high world, maybe even an immortal world.

"Apart from that, she is even hiding her true power. But as to how she had this technique, I am 100% sure it was from her master. The Celestial told me that whenever I meet someone with these flame runes on their body, I should protect them, that they are her disciples in a way.

"The Supreme called Purple Flame Lady is her direct disciple, and there is an unruly god running around with the same runes on her body, so I am sure this lady is the fourth or perhaps fifth generation Disciple of that Celestial."
On the battlefield, Lady Liora was merely waving her hand, sending powerful flame attacks at the vampires.
However, if one looked closely, one could see she was indeed holding herself back.
As to why she was doing that, only she knew.
"This is crazy. It is like the more we kill them, the stronger they become," Queen Jascia said, beheading a vampire.
Around her, thousands of vampires had died, with a few half-elves in the mix. However, as more continued to die, she began to sense the strength of the vampire still alive rising by the second.
And it wasn’t just her who noticed these changes. Many had already sensed this anomaly.
Vexthra narrowed her eyes when she also saw this. "The blood is powering them. If this goes on for long, many on our side will start dying."
She was about to send Velyra to handle the blood when Sylara rose into the air and formed a hand seal.
"Blood Transformation," she muttered coldly, causing thousands of vampires to pause and look at her.
"Kill her!" They charged toward her, weapons stabbing and swinging. However, just before they could get within five meters of her, Vaelros appeared, and a large chain formed a barrier around Sylara.
"There will be no stabbing today, fellas." With a wave of his hand, a thick chain came out of nowhere and slammed into the bodies of the hundreds of vampires charging at Sylara.
"Continue, Sylara. I will hold them back."
Sylara nodded and formed another hand seal. Suddenly, the blood on the battlefield started to move toward her.
Deep inside the crack, a three-meter-tall vampire, wielding a bow, looked in the direction of Sylara, and a frown appeared on his face.
Beside him were five others, each much more powerful than the vampires on the battlefield.
"Blood Transformation." His face paled. "She is using Blood Transformation."
The vampires who heard him turned and looked at Sylara in the distance. "How is she using Blood Transformation? Not even the Vampire King can use Blood Transformation."
This shock rippled across the thousands of vampires yet to arrive on the battlefield. Naturally, they knew what had to be done; however, they were hesitating.

Blood Transformation was a powerful skill among the vampires. It was said that during the Primordial Era, the original vampires had a technique that allowed them to create powerful seals using the blood of the slain.

It was said to be so powerful that the original vampires rose through the ranks, becoming one of the most powerful races in the universe. However, after the fall of the Primordial Era, the technique was lost.
But now, everyone was looking at the long-lost technique being used.
What was even worse was that the moment Sylara activated the Blood Transformation technique, the vampires lost their connection to the blood they were using to empower themselves.
"What should we do? It is said that if one’s bloodline is strong enough, killing someone who has the Blood Transformation has a slim chance of inheriting it.
"Among us, only the king has the bloodline and maybe some luck to claim it. Should we inform him?" one of them asked, but the look on the faces of everyone said otherwise.
"The king is busy at the moment, so calling him will be bad. However, how about we six go catch her and bring her to the king?"
"That is easier said than done. Don’t you see the terrifying chains around her and that horned brute protecting her? Getting close will be hard."
They all went back to staring at Sylara, hovering in the air with torrents of blood moving toward her. They hesitated, and then one of them moved.
However, before he could get close to the crack, his body halted, and he pulled back.
CRACK
The space split open, revealing the void. From within the void, six new figures emerged, bringing with them a powerful aura.
The thousands of vampires in line, including the three-meter-tall vampire who had spotted Sylara, went down on their knees and greeted the six figures. "We greet the Six Blood Royals."
The six vampires that arrived—four males and two females—were the Six Royals in charge of the Normal Vampire Army.
The moment they stepped out of the void, they looked coldly at Sylara, then a glint appeared in their eyes.
"Listen to order. Everyone should charge out. It is time to end this farce," the First Blood Prince said, pointing his spear forward.
He then turned to the five behind him and said, "Let’s get this over with."
They moved, and on the battlefield, everyone felt six powerful presences coming through the cracks

chapters.title: Chapter 902: The Apocalypse (6)
paragraphs: "Fall Back!"
Sect Leader Deimos shouted in a commanding tone, causing thousands of warriors to move back.

He sensed the six vampires coming through the crack, and so he commanded his people to fall back. Of course, even without him commanding them to fall back, they themselves could sense the dangers coming through the crack.
However, just when everyone was retreating, Zareth moved forward.
"Big sister, shouldn’t we go help them?" Unity asked. Vexthra shook her head.
"Per the details I have here, the six coming are the Six Blood Royals. They aren’t the strongest of the vampire race, so let’s allow Kaizo and Zareth to handle them.
The main danger will soon appear, and I need you all in full strength for it. Kent isn’t coming anytime soon, so we have to at least be able to save this world."
Unity nodded and focused her eyes on the crack in the air.

From within, the six people appeared with a powerful aura that immediately forced those who couldn’t move back much faster to go down on their knees. Some were coughing up blood, with a few passing out.
Thankfully, many were able to move back following Sect Leader Deimos’ command.

Zareth looked coldly at the new arrivals and smiled. "It will be best if you six focus on me instead of looking at her. Trust me, even if there are millions of you, getting to her will be next to impossible."
Instead of replying to him, one of the Six Blood Royals charged forward with a spear aimed at Zareth’s chest.
Zareth shook his head as a smile appeared on his face. "What an idiot."
He tapped his forehead with his index and middle finger and muttered coldly, "Petrifying Gaze."

A third eye opened on his forehead, resembling the eye of a serpent. Then, from within, a thin white light shot out and landed on the approaching Blood Prince’s body, turning him into a stone statue instantly.
His approach came to a sudden halt, and then lightning struck him.
"Explode for me."
Just when the fourth Blood Prince turned to stone, Kaizo’s fist went through his chest, turning him into chunks of rock.
The faces of the five remaining Blood Royals turned ashen as one of them was reduced to blocks of stone.
Kaizo floated beside Zareth and grinned at the five Blood Royals.
"It will be best if you all come at the same time. Don’t blame me for bullying you if you don’t heed by warning."
"Kill him."
The remaining five charged forward, their target now being Kaizo, who smiled and raised his hand, summoning a ring of golden lightning around them.
Zareth smirked and vanished from the ring of lightning. As for the five Blood Royals, they came to a halt when the ring appeared.
"No need to stop. The lightning ring only lowers your strength by 30%." With a grin on his face, Kaizo charged forward.
The five Blood Royals recovered from their shocked state and charged too. However, before they could get close to Kaizo, he vanished.
"Where did he go?" the First Blood Princess asked, looking around.
The others were doing the same. However, a few seconds later, Kaizo appeared through a strand of lightning and slammed his fist into the First Blood Princess’s face before vanishing again.

Meanwhile, the Blood Princess was hurled through the air, and just when she was about to touch the lightning ring, a powerful bolt of lightning, much thicker and deadlier, shot from the ring, drilling a hole through her forehead.
"I forgot to tell you, getting close to the ring is a death wish."
Kaizo appeared behind the Third Blood Prince, grabbed hold of both his hands, and hurled him forward.

The First Blood Prince reacted quickly, jumping forward to grab the Third Blood Prince. However, just when he was about to grab his leg, Kaizo appeared in the air and, using his knee, he slammed it hard into the First Blood Prince’s chin, causing a few teeth to fly out.
"Hope I didn’t get the fangs."
The First Blood Prince felt his world spin for a few seconds, but he recovered when a painful cry came from one side of the ring.
When he turned and looked, he saw the Third Blood Prince’s body letting out smoke as he fell to his death. The ring barbecued him to death.
In that very moment, the First Blood Prince and the remaining Blood Royals felt they had fallen into the trap of a monster who wasn’t even taking them seriously.
Naturally, Kaizo wasn’t taking them seriously, for regardless of how powerful they were, Kaizo had faced those several times stronger than them.
So they were mere bugs before him.
On the battlefield, the warriors had retreated far back, keeping the vampires on one side of the battlefield.
Naturally, everything had come to a halt, with everyone looking at Kaizo and the Blood Royals.
All vampires under the command of the six blood royals were on the battlefield, but none were attacking.
Far in the distance, Vexthra raised her brow when she sensed something coming from within the crack. She used the connection to send a message to Princess Lovina and Alina.
"End the battle."
They nodded.
Princess Lovina moved forward and raised her staff. "Time to end this." Her staff shone purple as her poison energy moved through it.
"Poison World."
A thick purple mist came from her staff and rose up, forming into a portal. Then, from the portal, more purple mist appeared and began forming into more portals.
Princess Lovina waved her staff and muttered some strange words. However, when she finished, balls of black mist came from the thousands of portals that appeared in the air.
"Grand Battle Formation—Activate."
At the moment the balls appear, the busty Alina also made her move.
Up in the air, a blue formation housing hundreds of smaller formations appeared and swallowed the black mists that Princess Lovina had summoned.
"First Formation: Battleground Movement."
Just when the vampires were looking up, a formation appeared on the ground, and black mist enveloped them, causing many to start coughing.
"What is this?" one vampire shouted, feeling her body giving up on her.
"Retreat," she called for a retreat. However, before any of them could move, Alina activated the second and third formations.
"Space Lock."
"Earth Movement."
From all sides, the ground started moving.
Those who attempted to fly felt something restricting them, forcing them to stay on the ground. However, those who were moving or managing to move felt the ground give up on them.
It was as if, for every step they took, three more were added to the distance between them and the crack. And while all this was happening, the mist was spreading among them.
After enveloping 80% of them, Princess Lovina smiled and waved her staff.
"Poison Reversal."
All those within the poison mist came to a standstill, and then, as if they had eaten bad food, they all started vomiting blood.
"What in the hell?"
Lady Enzi muttered, looking at the vampires vomiting blood, with some dropping dead as their bodies began drying up.
"Just what kind of monsters are these people?" She looked from Princess Lovina to Kaizo and back, and all she could see were monsters that she couldn’t measure up to.
Within minutes, 80% of the vampire army was turned to blood, and all of the blood was being channeled by Sylara, who was still hovering in the air.
The warriors were left staring at all this with shocked expressions.
By the time the poison managed to reach 90% of the vampires, the rest vanished back into the crack.
Vexthra looked at Unity. "Time for you to shine."
"Finally."
Unity vanished and appeared beside Alina, causing the warriors on the ground to turn toward her.
However, Unity’s focus was on the crack. She took out an arrow that, the moment she brought it out, everyone, regardless of strength level, felt the danger within.
Vexthra shook her head, looking at the arrow in Unity’s hand. "Mercy on those vampires."
Unity placed the arrow in her bow and pulled back, aiming at the crack.

chapters.title: Chapter 903: The Apocalypse (7)
paragraphs: [30 Minutes Before Unity’s Arrow Entered Through the Crack – The Dead Region – Core Area]
Thirty minutes ago, during the attack on Sonox by the Sea Race, Amix, the leader of the Hand, met with the Vampire King.
This meeting was one that would require great sacrifice. However, knowing the benefit that would come from it, the Vampire King, who was after greatness, chose to follow through with the plan.

This plan, of course, was the ritual meant to open the Doors of the Apocalypse. However, instead of those doors opening, the Forsaken Doors would open. This, of course, means danger is slowly coming to Sonox.
"Like I said earlier, the moment the doors open, you and your people will be rewarded with so much you cannot even begin to imagine.

I have already promised to deliver the blood of the Wynthralls. Even though the ones I delivered are not up to standard, the moment my people are free, I will be sure to hunt down the true bloodline and give them to you and the core family."
The Vampire King, a handsome man with two red horns and bat wings, nodded at Amix.
"I will allow my first strike force to attack should the Sea Race fail. Not that they can do much, considering they are weaklings.
However, I expect this ritual to end before they are overrun. Though I don’t mind them all dying, my second strike force will only be deployed if we have to.

As for the Royal Vampire Force, I will seal the crack before I let them fight your battle. The human continent is unguarded, and I can conquer it while I slowly find resources to get off this food-forsaken planet.
So be sure to hurry before I am forced to end everything."

Amix nodded, though she was not happy being threatened. However, since she had no other choice but to work with the vampires, she swallowed her anger and flew away to start the ritual. It would take 45 minutes maximum.
The Vampire King was seated on a blood-red throne in a large hall, where ten vampires with the same features as the Vampire King could be seen.
On the outside, 40,000 vampires of the same nature stood radiating a powerful aura. Their aura is much more powerful than that of regular vampires.
Ten kilometers away from them, 200,000 vampires with much shorter horns and no wings also stood radiating similar auras.
Then, 50 kilometers from them, the pale-looking vampires were geared up and staring at the crack that was slowly forming.
In the vampire race, these pale vampires are those without powerful bloodlines. Their leaders are the six Blood Royals and the six Grand Generals.
They are just normal vampires. The 200,000 with horns but no wings are known as the Elite Vampires, while those with horns and wings are regarded as the Royal Vampires.

Thirty minutes later, the crack opened, and the vampires had long attacked. However, while the vampires had no plans to go all out, plans changed when the six Blood Royals in charge of the normal vampires attacked.

This action forced the Elite Vampires to sense something was amiss, so they chose to check it out. That was when they discovered the treasure that had appeared on the battlefield, causing them to make a decision.
One of them, against all odds, ran to the core of the Dead Region where only the Royal Vampires lived.
"Stop right there." Just as he was approaching, a voice forced him to stop. "What do you want in the core region?" one of the Royal Vampires asked.
"I would like to report that someone with Blood Transformation abilities has appeared on the battlefield, and also, 90% of the normal vampires have been killed."
"What?"

The moment the words came out of his mouth, the Elite Vampire lost control of his body as he was pulled by an invisible force. The next second, he appeared in the large hall, kneeling before the Vampire King.
"What did you just say?"
The King asked, causing the Elite Vampire to turn pale.
"There is someone using Blood Transformation..." The moment the words came out of his mouth, he dropped dead.
"All Elite Vampires should move out." The Vampire King’s voice boomed, spreading far and wide. "Catch the one using the Blood Transformation alive."
All Elite Vampires moved the moment the order came.
However, just as they were charging toward the crack, they saw a brilliant red light pass through it and was heading toward them.
One of the six Elite vampire generals leading the charge leapt into the air with a powerful spear, aiming to destroy the arrow.
However, just as his spear was about to meet the arrow, it vanished, and a large formation appeared in the air and on the ground.
That was when they heard a sweet voice speak from the other side of the crack.
"Cataclysmic Arrow: Explode."
The land they stood on shook, and then from within the formation in the sky, a very large, metallic, and deadly arrow appeared in an instant and embedded itself in the ground.
"BOOM."
Unity mouthed the word as the arrow exploded, turning the very ground all the vampires stood on to explode into stones and sand.
Thousands were instantly turned to ash, with thousands more sustaining injuries that were impossible to recover from.
Unity laughed, giving thumbs up to her two Primordial Spirits. They made the arrow...
Inside the large hall, the Vampire King rose from his chair and vanished. When he appeared, half of his 200,000 Elite Vampires were either ash or screaming on the ground.
His expression turned ashen when he saw this.

His gaze was directed at the crack leading to Sonox. However, before he could make up his mind, a beauty holding a bow stepped through, followed by a titan brute whose body was covered in golden lightning armor.
Kaizo looked at the Vampire King and smiled. "From the look on your face, I can tell you are very angry. I wonder what you are going to do about it."
"I also want to see what he is going to do about it," Unity muttered, spinning an arrow between her fingers as she stared at the Vampire King.
In no time, the Royal Vampires appeared behind the Vampire King, causing the very weather to start turning dark.

"Looks like you guys were looking down on us. Who could have predicted there are more of you here, and even much more powerful than those idiots you sent out?" Zareth spoke as a dragon roar came through the crack.
He arrived standing on the head of the Void Dragon.
"More to kill, I suppose." Vaelros also appeared, his fist coated in thick chains.
Princess Lovina and Alina arrived as well. Sect Leader Deimos, Lady Enzi, Lady Liora, and the sect Elders also came through the crack.
But it didn’t end there. The various Kings and some of their capable warriors appeared. Though they numbered only a few hundred for each kingdom, they knew that doing nothing would look bad for them.
Even the core disciples and some inner disciples, who included Nyss and Kent’s friends, chose to join the offensive and enter the Dead Region.

By the time every one of them had joined, the army behind Kaizo and Unity now numbered slightly over ten thousand, while their opponents still numbered over 140,000, with powerful vampires now joining the mix.
The only one still to enter was Sylara, who was almost done absorbing the blood on the outside for her Blood Transformation.
"Kill them," the Vampire King muttered coldly.
The Royal Vampires and the Elite Vampires charged forward.
However, just as they were about to clash, an ear-shattering sound came from the distance, halting everyone.

chapters.title: Chapter 904: The Apocalypse (8)
paragraphs: The charge that came from both sides came to a halt in an instant.
Every last person turned toward the direction of the sound, and for a moment, they all broke into a cold sweat.
A large red door, about 4 km high and 10 km wide, was slowly opening with an oppressive and forbidden aura. The more it opened, the more sinister the aura coming from within.

As it opened halfway, every last person standing in the air was forced to land on the ground. The only ones that remained were the Vampire King, a few royal vampires, Lady Enzi, a few elders from the sect, Kent’s undead Legion, and his wives, who were currently present on the battlefield.
Some of the kings and queens in Sonox, along with their ancestors, also remained in the air. Not even the five-seeded core disciples remained in the air.
The pressure was too much for them to do anything but land.
"What is that?" Unity asked, pointing at the door.
"That is the Forsaken Door." Vexthra appeared through the crack, bringing with her all of her sisters and Kent’s Legion, including the Bloodvein Tribe.
"Big sister, what is the Forsaken Door?" Unity turned to Vexthra, and so did everyone else.

"The Forsaken Door is like a portal that opens to the Forsaken Race. Basically, when this door is fully opened, the Forsaken Race will come through, and the first thing they will do is slaughter everyone, including children.
Naturally, this world is coming to an end if we don’t fight back."
"Tch, talk for yourself. Forsaken Race or not, they are my allies, and so I don’t even have to worry about you all. In the end, you all will perish like you should have 25,000 years ago."
The Vampire King laughed, his voice echoing across the landscape as he stared at the faces of the warriors of Sonox.

"What an idiot," Vexthra spoke, causing the Vampire King to stop his laughter. He frowned at Vexthra, but deep within his heart, he knew that moving for an attack would lead to his doom, so he merely stood back and pointed at her.
"Keep running your mouth bitch. When they come, I will be sure to enjoy watching you choke on your own blood."

"I think I will be the one to enjoy watching that. After all, if what I know about the Forsaken Race is true, the first people they kill whenever they invade a world are those who helped them get there.
In this context, you idiots helped open the door, and knowing only the blood of the cursed can seal it again, they will kill you or enslave you and use you to open more doors in the future.
Also, even if you manage to escape, because you aided a Forsaken Race in breaking their world-bound curse, the heavens will punish you severely.
Basically, the only chance you have at surviving now is either to face them and hope you survive or just wait for death."
Vexthra, being a goddess and the first wife of a genius named Kent, felt like talking to the Vampire King was beneath her, so she turned toward Sect Leader Deimos, Lady Enzi, and Lady Liora.

"My name is Vexthra, a Flame Demon and the first wife of Kent." The three looked at each other, unsure why they felt the need to bow before Vexthra. The issue about her being Kent’s wife wasn’t even registered in their heads, for the sight of her alone mesmerized them.
’Maybe I still don’t have enough handle on my divine aura,’ Vexthra smiled in her head.
"Kent is not here now, and as the three strongest in charge of this world, I want you to mobilize only the able warriors you think can fight those above the Core Formation stage."
Lady Enzi frowned, hearing Vexthra’s words. "Are you saying the beings coming are above the Core Formation stage?"

"Yes. The Forsaken Race is only found in the High World and above, so naturally, those coming will be above the Core Formation stage. And the painful part is, they will not be restricted by this world’s limits.
So be quick with that, for the survival of this world hangs in the balance."
Vexthra then turned to Kaizo. "You will lead the charge, and please, know that until the last one of them is slaughtered, the battle will not end."
"Don’t worry, big sister, I will be sure to send these suckers to hell."
Vexthra just smiled. If it were up to her, she would have chosen Neomi to lead the charge against the forsaken race. However, the quest stated that Kaizo was to lead it.
She did not know why he was selected, but she trusted the orders of the universe, and so she would not disobey.
Sect Leader Deimos turned to the warriors of Sonox and began making sure every last one of them knew the danger that was coming.

However, even after knowing the danger, every last one of them chose to stay and fight for their world. He wanted to use force to send away those he knew did not have the means to fight. However, in the end, he chose to let them stay.
Meanwhile, Lady Enzi and Liora moved to the side. "Are you sure you don’t want to leave?" Lady Enzi asked.

Lady Liora sighed deeply and then shook her head. "This is the world of my disciple. It is in danger, meaning my disciple is in danger. If I leave without at least doing anything to save it, how would I face my master then?"
"But you have really tried over the past years to reach where you are now. Are you sure you want to throw that away?"
Lady Liora smiled. "My dear friend, one of the reasons why I chose to join the Midnight Shadows was to fight for the right cause, like my lord, the Faceless Assassin, did millions of years ago.
This is a righteous cause, and so, as much as I would love to walk away from the light, the battle coming requires both Lady Liora and the Silent Angel."
Lady Enzi sighed and then nodded.
"Just be careful, and don’t get swallowed by the chaos."

As the only person who knew Lady Liora’s true identity, she was worried about her friend. Though Lady Liora chose to let go this once and try to save this world, Lady Enzi already knew how this would end, and so she was prepared to do everything in her power to ensure her friend was safe after all this was over.
The door continued to open, with only a few inches left before it fully opened.
"Be ready, everyone. It is going to be a deadly battle." Kaizo smiled, ready for what was coming.
A few seconds later, the door opened, and a Peak Spirit Emperor stepped through, unleashing her presence.
The moment all eyes fell on her, the resolve to join the battle was shattered, and many began running away.
Vexthra shook her head but said nothing.
"I will only say this once: surrender, and you might live a few more days. Resist, and every living soul in this world will die..." The lady spoke coldly, causing many to take a few steps back.
The Vampire King flew forward and knelt on the ground. "This humble servant was the one who aided in opening the door. Please, have mercy on my race."
The lady looked at the Vampire King coldly and waved her hand. "Kill the cursed ones first."
The ground began shaking the next second, bringing a smile to Kaizo’s face. He looked toward Alina and smiled.
"Alina, I need her head."

chapters.title: Chapter 905: The Apocalypse (9)
paragraphs: The Forsaken Race isn’t exactly ugly.

If anything, the thousands charging toward Kaizo and his team are rather good-looking. Most have white skin with red horns, just like the faces that have been appearing in the mirror whenever Amix calls the one she refers to as her mother.

They are not pale like the normal vampires. They just have white skin with red horns and imposing heights. Among the thousands who charged forward, 30% are at the Core Formation stage, with the rest ranging between Spirit Ascension and Spirit King.
"How are we going to survive this?" an inner disciple said as he turned and ran away.
If only they knew running wouldn’t take them anywhere, they would have waited for their death—or at least stayed to see what Alina was capable of.
Alina was the only person who charged forward, surprising everyone who had gathered the courage to stand their ground and fight the forsaken race.
Vexthra, who was watching Kaizo, wondered what he was planning by sending only Alina forward. She wanted to see if giving the helm to Kaizo was the right thing or the wrong call.
Alina moved and stopped when she was far enough away from her team. With a flick of her hand, a disc-shaped item appeared.
The items have runic markings on them, with each showing a deadly combination of arrays ready to be unleashed.
"This will be enough to cause some chaos."
A smile appeared on her face as she channeled her energy into it.
The moment her energy entered the disc, a formation emerged from within and rose into the air. Alina didn’t immediately activate it like she did with the previous ones.
She took out a small rune brush and drew runes quickly in the air before sending them flying into the larger formation.
All this happened within seconds, but by the time the Forsaken Race warriors came within 2 km of her, Alina had already completed her formation.
"Eternal Darkness."
The formation expanded, and in an instant, the 20 km radius around the Forsaken Race warriors was plunged into perpetual darkness.
This kind of darkness was absolute.
"Nice one, Alina." Kaizo then turned to Vari, Lani, and the other assassins in the legion. "I really need her head."
Vexthra raised her brow, impressed by the brilliance of Kaizo’s move.
’He is smart. Very smart to come up with such a move.’ She knew that in this very moment, inside the formation, every last Forsaken warrior was blinded both in sight and in senses.
Even their ears can’t hear anything.
Naturally, this gave way for the assassins in the legion to do their unholy work.

"Hahahaha!" Lani’s laughter filled the air as she moved through the shadows, wielding her dagger. Vari was the same, but instead of using her white haired form, which is regarded as her holy or justice side, she was clad in black, with even her pupils dark as she moved.
This shows she was coming for their lives, and she doesn’t need any justification to claim them.

Inside the darkness, Lani appeared behind a Spirit King who, despite being in such close proximity, only managed to sense a calm presence, but before he could identify where it came from, his head came rolling.
Lani wasted no time and moved to the next, her laughter echoing through the darkness. Soon, heads began rolling.
Vari was no different. Wherever she passed, heads fell.
Nyxira, one of the deadliest assassins in Elsa’s Soul Sentinels, was also within the darkness, where she could clearly see her targets.
However, unlike Vari and Lani, she wasn’t going for the kill. Instead, she was merely placing marks on enemies before moving away.
She had a deadly ability that required her to mark her targets in the same way Nyss also marks hers.
Within the span of five minutes, thousands lay dead, with many still struggling to escape the darkness.
Far in the distance, the lady who had given the command to charge frowned. "That is a Tier 14 formation... just where did that formation expert come from?"
Amix, who was standing beside the lady, looked in the direction of Alina and frowned. She didn’t know where she came from, and that alone was something nobody wanted.
Knowing nothing about your enemy is always bad.
"I don’t know where she came from, but I have a way to kill her." Amix retrieved a vial from her space ring and handed it to the lady.
"This is the Heart-Exploding Poison. We just have to get close to her, and she will die screaming." The lady took the poison and looked toward Alina.

"The main strike force will be coming out in the next ten minutes. The moment they get here, all of this farce will be over. However, if we don’t do anything before these ten minutes are up, every last warrior will die."
The lady looked at the darkness before her, and her anger boiled even more.
"But then again, if we let them all die, then the chances of using the bodies for whatever we have planned for the vampires will be even more deadly."
Amix, who wasn’t expecting the lady to abandon her men in battle, frowned slightly; however, before she could say anything, the lady pushed her, sending her flying back several meters.
Right where Amix had stood, a dark figure appeared like smoke and stabbed her dagger at the lady, who used her superior cultivation base to evade by leaping back.
However, when she landed, she felt her leg sink, and she was swallowed by darkness.
Far in the distance, Elyndra, Kent’s fifth undead and also the strongest in the legion, formed a seal right as the lady emerged from another path of darkness.
"Space Lock."
In an instant, the 10 km radius around them was locked down.
"Where am I?" the lady asked, looking around. Her eyes landed on a beauty with silvery-white hair, and her anger burst out. She charged forward, stabbing a sword that appeared in her hand at Elyndra.
However, the undead beauty merely smiled and waved her hand. "Spatial Descent: Infinity Fall."
The stabbing strike came to a halt, and then the lady felt her body start falling. "What is this?"
She panicked, unsure why she was falling, yet she wasn’t hitting the ground. Even worse, she tried to use the void, but she felt her surroundings locked, preventing her from opening it.
"I need her head!" Kaizo, who still hadn’t received the head, shouted.
However, no one minded him, for they knew assassinating a Peak Spirit Emperor wasn’t something they could do...
Well, assassinating a Peak Spirit Emperor wasn’t something that could be achieved easily. However, among Kent’s undead, there was one who had the means to kill the Peak Spirit Emperor’s lady.
Naturally, she was the first to move, even before Kaizo gave the command.

So when the third command came from Kaizo, Velmora, who was hidden inside the Forsaken lady’s shadow, emerged, and with one swift swing of her deadly scythe, the Spirit Emperor lady, someone said to be above them all, lost her head, shocking everyone.
Lady Liora, who was standing beside Lady Enzi, raised her brow. "Shadow Displacement," she muttered, unsure how to feel at the moment.

sentences.text: The Forsaken Race isn’t exactly ugly.
If anything, the thousands charging toward Kaizo and his team are rather good-looking.
Most have white skin with red horns, just like the faces that have been appearing in the mirror whenever Amix calls the one she refers to as her mother.
They are not pale like the normal vampires.
They just have white skin with red horns and imposing heights.
Among the thousands who charged forward, 30% are at the Core Formation stage, with the rest ranging between Spirit Ascension and Spirit King.
"How are we going to survive this?" an inner disciple said as he turned and ran away.
If only they knew running wouldn’t take them anywhere, they would have waited for their death—or at least stayed to see what Alina was capable of.
Alina was the only person who charged forward, surprising everyone who had gathered the courage to stand their ground and fight the forsaken race.
Vexthra, who was watching Kaizo, wondered what he was planning by sending only Alina forward.
She wanted to see if giving the helm to Kaizo was the right thing or the wrong call.
Alina moved and stopped when she was far enough away from her team.
With a flick of her hand, a disc-shaped item appeared.
The items have runic markings on them, with each showing a deadly combination of arrays ready to be unleashed.
"This will be enough to cause some chaos."
A smile appeared on her face as she channeled her energy into it.
The moment her energy entered the disc, a formation emerged from within and rose into the air.
Alina didn’t immediately activate it like she did with the previous ones.
She took out a small rune brush and drew runes quickly in the air before sending them flying into the larger formation.
All this happened within seconds, but by the time the Forsaken Race warriors came within 2 km of her, Alina had already completed her formation.
"Eternal Darkness."
The formation expanded, and in an instant, the 20 km radius around the Forsaken Race warriors was plunged into perpetual darkness.
This kind of darkness was absolute.
"Nice one, Alina." Kaizo then turned to Vari, Lani, and the other assassins in the legion.
"I really need her head."
Vexthra raised her brow, impressed by the brilliance of Kaizo’s move.
’He is smart.
Very smart to come up with such a move.’ She knew that in this very moment, inside the formation, every last Forsaken warrior was blinded both in sight and in senses.
Even their ears can’t hear anything.
Naturally, this gave way for the assassins in the legion to do their unholy work.
"Hahahaha!" Lani’s laughter filled the air as she moved through the shadows, wielding her dagger.
Vari was the same, but instead of using her white haired form, which is regarded as her holy or justice side, she was clad in black, with even her pupils dark as she moved.
This shows she was coming for their lives, and she doesn’t need any justification to claim them.

Inside the darkness, Lani appeared behind a Spirit King who, despite being in such close proximity, only managed to sense a calm presence, but before he could identify where it came from, his head came rolling.
Lani wasted no time and moved to the next, her laughter echoing through the darkness.
Soon, heads began rolling.
Vari was no different.
Wherever she passed, heads fell.
Nyxira, one of the deadliest assassins in Elsa’s Soul Sentinels, was also within the darkness, where she could clearly see her targets.
However, unlike Vari and Lani, she wasn’t going for the kill.
Instead, she was merely placing marks on enemies before moving away.
She had a deadly ability that required her to mark her targets in the same way Nyss also marks hers.
Within the span of five minutes, thousands lay dead, with many still struggling to escape the darkness.
Far in the distance, the lady who had given the command to charge frowned.
"That is a Tier 14 formation... just where did that formation expert come from?"
Amix, who was standing beside the lady, looked in the direction of Alina and frowned.
She didn’t know where she came from, and that alone was something nobody wanted.
Knowing nothing about your enemy is always bad.
"I don’t know where she came from, but I have a way to kill her." Amix retrieved a vial from her space ring and handed it to the lady.
"This is the Heart-Exploding Poison.
We just have to get close to her, and she will die screaming." The lady took the poison and looked toward Alina.
"The main strike force will be coming out in the next ten minutes.
The moment they get here, all of this farce will be over.
However, if we don’t do anything before these ten minutes are up, every last warrior will die."
The lady looked at the darkness before her, and her anger boiled even more.
"But then again, if we let them all die, then the chances of using the bodies for whatever we have planned for the vampires will be even more deadly."
Amix, who wasn’t expecting the lady to abandon her men in battle, frowned slightly; however, before she could say anything, the lady pushed her, sending her flying back several meters.
Right where Amix had stood, a dark figure appeared like smoke and stabbed her dagger at the lady, who used her superior cultivation base to evade by leaping back.
However, when she landed, she felt her leg sink, and she was swallowed by darkness.

chapters.title: Chapter 906: The Apocalypse (10)
paragraphs: Nobody knew when Velmora slipped into the lady’s shadow.
In fact, even Vexthra, although not a goddess at the moment, had a much higher divine sense than everyone present. But even she didn’t know when Velmora made her move.
Perhaps the only one who knew something about what happened was Lady Liora, who managed to figure out part of the process after the head of the Spirit Emperor came rolling.

Naturally, the move Velmora used was one she had prepared ahead of time. She is an Assassin who thrives in secrecy. So she made her move that thinking about it now, they all felt their scalps go numb.
Right when the door was opening, at the exact moment it started sending out powerful auras, Velmora saw an opening appear in the lady’s defense, allowing her to use a skill only Liora recognized.
’Shadow Displacement’
The skill allowed her to swap shadows with the lady.
The lady’s shadow came to her, and hers went to the lady, allowing her to move and appear instantly whenever she wanted.
So she waited, and just when the lady was working out a plan against Alina, Velmora knew her time had come. So she attacked Amix, which was a decoy for the main attack.
What she never expected was Elyndra trapping the lady. Trapping her was like 80% of her work has been lifted off her.

The only thing left was for the lady now trapped in the ’Space Lock’ to focus on her captor, while Velmora, who had sharpened her scythe back when she was training in Fedora, was more than ready to continue her unholy beheading.
It all played out just as she had planned it with an added sauce.
"Just how did she get there?" Unity muttered, looking at Velmora, who picked up the head and threw it at Kaizo.
The unruly Kaizo caught it and stored it in his space ring.
"Something seems to be blocking them from coming, so why don’t we kill them all before the big guns appear?"
Half of the legion moved, and soon, the slaughter that the forsaken race never saw coming descended on them.
The sect elders and the various kings and queens could only stand and watch as Kent’s ladies and legion rapidly slaughtered the forsaken warriors as if their cultivation bases weren’t even a factor.
In no time, they killed every last one, with only Amix taken alive.
"This is just the first phase or more of a show of what is to come. This time, you all should be ready." With that, Vexthra vanished back to the tower for everyone’s safety.

If she were to stay, the chances of her joining the battle would be high, and while having a goddess on their side would be ideal, her mere presence in the battle would bring doom to everyone. So it was best if she wasn’t there at all.
However, with the tower’s overpowered abilities, watching what was happening on the outside in real-time was a mere wave away.
Alina deactivated the formation and immediately started setting up the next one for the next phase of the battle.
Meanwhile, on the other side of the large door, thousands of warriors ranging from Spirit Ascension upward stood ready, watching the green portal slowly turn red like the color on the other side.
The moment it turned red, they would move and begin the invasion. If any of them were to go now, they would lose their cultivation base by one stage.
Though just one, none wanted to do that—or more like their leaders didn’t want them to drop by a stage—so they sent ten thousand to clear the way.
The world was vast, and the sky was painted in a gloomy gray hue. Around the planet, if one were to look from the outside, there was a green ring filled with countless restrictions.
These restrictions were placed there to prevent anyone on this planet from leaving.
However, this restriction was proven null when the Forsaken door opened. It was like whatever authority the restriction had was broken by the forsaken door.
Inside a large building, ten people, all at the Heavenly Ascension stage, were seated, watching a projection of green dots turning red at a rapid pace.
Among the ten, one lady sat in a much more extravagant seat, clearly showing she was the leader of the nine. Naturally, her level 5 Heavenly Ascension stage cultivation shows she was the strongest.
Of course, if Amix were present, he would have been happy to finally meet the lady she called her mother.

They called her the Forsaken Queen Deva. She was the sole reason the invasion was possible. Though she couldn’t leave her world, there were many loopholes that allowed her to worm her way into the heads of innocent beings in the vast universe.
One of them was Amix, the leader of the Hand.
"It seems the people of that world are much stronger than we gave them credit for," Deva said, looking at the rapidly changing green dots.
"Does this mean they have what it takes to counter us?" one of them, a level 3 Heavenly Ascension stage Forsaken warrior, asked.
"Don’t be ridiculous, Boris. We are a high world, and they are a medium-low standard world. What makes you think they have the means to face the kind of army we have on the outside?
Even if they were a high world, with the force we have under us, with the force I command, this invasion will be a success. We cannot fail, not when the others are counting on us."
Deva kept staring at the dots until a deep green one suddenly turned red. Her expression shifted instantly.
"They were able to kill a Peak Spirit Emperor, meaning they are not simple. We have to destroy them once and for all."
She looked toward the direction of the portal leading to Sonox and issued an order.
"All Spirit Emperors, charge out when the portal is red. After that, follow the previous setup."
Over twenty thousand Spirit Emperors flew into the air and prepared for the portal to turn pure red.
On the other side, Alina had tens of thousands of runes in the air. They moved and merged into a massive formation on both the ground and in the sky.

"They will be here soon, so be ready. And like I said, if you can’t face them, retreat," Kaizo shouted before moving to the front of the line. Beside him stood Uncle Drake, who had taken his full dragon form and was ready for battle.

Behind them stood Kent’s ladies and his legion. Then there was the Bloodvein tribe led by tribe chief Malthar. And finally, behind the legion were the Supreme Immortal Sect Elders and the disciples, with a few warriors from Sonox who chose to stay.

Among them were Lady Aelith, Lord Qilin, Queen Jascia, King Thalirion, and several others. This was their world, and running away before the enemy even arrived was not something they planned on doing.

On one side, the Vampires were locked inside a formation that Alina had trapped them in. She could not allow them to retreat back to Sonox when the core of the world’s power was facing a much greater threat.
Asha was hovering over them.
"They are almost here." The light in Kaizo’s eyes burned fiercely as he stared at the portal.
"Charge!"
With that, Kaizo moved, and so did Uncle Drake—right at the moment the Forsaken warriors arrived.

chapters.title: Chapter 907: The Apocalypse (11)
paragraphs: "Mountain Breaking Punch"
Kaizo landed hard, his fist crackling with golden lightning as he punched out, striking the chest of a Spirit Lord. The Spirit Emperor was sent flying several meters away.
However, Kaizo wasn’t done. He moved, and before the Spirit Emperor could land on the ground, his fist connected with his back, breaking his spine.
A painful cry came from the Spirit Emperor, who couldn’t bear that the battle had not even truly begun, yet he was already overpowered by a mere core formation stage brute.
But his nightmare didn’t end there.
Just as his body was about to touch the ground, a faint shadow portal appeared, and the Spirit Emperor fell in, only to reappear with a dagger just an inch away from his forehead.
Vari drove her dagger through the Spirit Emperor’s forehead.
His vision turned dark, and then he fell to the ground. Not far from her, Irina also beheaded another Spirit Emperor and was off to the next.

One might wonder just how Core Formation experts were killing Spirit Lords. Naturally, none of this should have been possible. There was no way a small world like Sonox should have this many terrifying warriors.

However, Alina was on the battlefield, and while she could write a restriction to limit the cultivation base of the forsaken warriors to the Core Formation stage, that was just too darn time-consuming and too powerful to maintain.
So she was able to write one that gave her side an upper hand when it came to pinpointing the weak points of the enemies.
The formation she had opened and was pouring all her energy into was doing three things. The first was the speed boost.

Every last warrior on her side had three times their speed, which was enough to match the speed of the enemy, especially the assassins and archers on the battlefield, who were known for their swiftness.

The second, of course, was quick teleportation. It was what was draining the most energy. However, it was set up in such a way that if a teammate was severely injured, they would be teleported outside of the battlefield.
It was absolute, but effective.
It was also draining her.
However, the last effect was the Weak Point Identifier. It was, in a way, like Kent’s Soul Map, but much weaker, yet still effective.
It was pointing out the weak points of the enemy, allowing her teammates to deal the most lethal blows.
Veydris popped out of the void and stabbed his sword through the shoulder of a Spirit Emperor before slipping back into the void.
"Poison Explosion!"
Princess Lovina activated a poison skill, and from the wound left by Veydris, along with others left by her teammates, green lotuses started growing.
All those with cuts on them were immediately brought to a halt. However, none managed to figure out what was happening before powerful explosions started sounding across the battlefield.

Some lost their arms, lower halves of their bodies, limbs, and much more. Many also died, but Princess Lovina alone wasn’t enough to commit mass slaughter, so Elaine chose to become death instead of life.
She floated in the air, and behind her, a large tree housing thousands of thin leaves appeared, exuding a powerful death qi.
She pointed forward and mouthed the skill name, "Leaves of Death."
The tree shook violently, then, like bees, the leaves came off their branches and surged forward, cutting through the Spirit Emperor like swords.

Of course, the leaves alone weren’t enough to kill them. However, Elaine, too, wasn’t going for the kill immediately. Her plan had something to do with the many graves inside her Life and Death space.
Until then, she was simply doing her part to handle as many Spirit Emperors as she could.
Soon, the Spirit Emperors started getting mixed with Spirit King experts and Spirit Ascension forsaken warriors.
However, while that wasn’t exactly a good thing, the moment they appeared, Kaizo called out to Sylara, who was still on the outside, transforming the blood.
A few seconds later, she appeared in the distance, overlooking the battlefield.
Unity flew toward her. "How much longer until you are done?"
Sylara examined her body for a few seconds before answering, "Twenty more minutes. I have already formed the seal and am now fusing it with my soul."
"Better hurry, because we are outnumbered and overpowered here. Without you, we wouldn’t be able to handle them. The least we can do is hold them back if some of us go all out."
"I will do my best."
Unity nodded and flew away, raining down arrows on the Forsaken warriors.

Kaizo and Uncle Drake were at the front of the battlefield, clashing with many Spirit Lords. Naturally, Kaizo was using 5% of his bloodline, and so was Uncle Drake, so while they weren’t killing like their teammates, all the Peak Spirit Emperors were on them.

Kaizo was surrounded by five Peak Spirit Emperors, and so was Uncle Drake, but despite being overpowered, they kept getting back up. Since the enemy wasn’t about to ignore them and focus on the others, they weren’t having it easy at all.
The Seven Sea Kings held back Uncle Drake because he fought them at 10% of his power. Anything higher, and he would have killed thousands, which would have included his own teammates.
However, things were different now.
The battlefield was open on all sides, and Uncle Drake could see only Forsaken warriors. This made him start to fight more destructively, like a dragon should.
The enemy knew the damage he could cause, so they were going all out to stop him.
"How much higher can you go, Uncle Drake?" Kaizo asked, taking a sword swing with his hand, which was coated in a red metallic gauntlet.
"I can go as high as fifteen, but that will drain me rapidly. However, just five is already good enough to hold these idiots back."
Kaizo laughed, landing a kick in a Forsaken warrior’s gut. "I know, right? They are much weaker than I expected."
"Very weak. If I were to go up to seven, I am confident I can crush one’s head like a tomato."
"Why don’t you do it, Uncle Drake?"
"Are you sure?"
"I am. I want to see a head pop."
"Very well."
Uncle Drake rose into the air, causing the Forsaken warriors to sense something was amiss, so they flew toward him, aiming to stop the annoying dragon at all costs.
"Idiots," Kaizo muttered coldly. Then the heavens churned, and the clouds turned red and black. From the clouds, a large black dragon moved, sending down a powerful pressure.
"Yi Lai, now."
The moment Kaizo spoke, Kent’s Dragon Necromancer appeared with her sword raised.
"Forbidden Art," she spoke in a sinister tone, causing the clouds to churn and thunder to rumble across the sky.
The Peak Spirit Emperors who chased after Uncle Drake turned and looked at Yi Lai, sensing something very bad was about to happen.

"It is rude to turn your back on your enemy." Uncle Drake, now in his human form, appeared behind one of the Spirit Emperors and grabbed his head, sinking his claws through his forehead and around his skull.
’Pop!’
With a pop, the Spirit Lord’s head was crushed like a tomato.
At the same time, Yi Lai was also ready...
"First Form: Domain Sealing Strike."
"Nooooo..."

Until then, she was simply doing her part to handle as many Spirit Emperors as she could.
Soon, the Spirit Emperors started getting mixed with Spirit King experts and Spirit Ascension forsaken warriors.
However, while that wasn’t exactly a good thing, the moment they appeared, Kaizo called out to Sylara, who was still on the outside, transforming the blood.
A few seconds later, she appeared in the distance, overlooking the battlefield.
Unity flew toward her.
"How much longer until you are done?"
Sylara examined her body for a few seconds before answering, "Twenty more minutes.
I have already formed the seal and am now fusing it with my soul."
"Better hurry, because we are outnumbered and overpowered here.
Without you, we wouldn’t be able to handle them.
The least we can do is hold them back if some of us go all out."
"I will do my best."
Unity nodded and flew away, raining down arrows on the Forsaken warriors.
Kaizo and Uncle Drake were at the front of the battlefield, clashing with many Spirit Lords.
Naturally, Kaizo was using 5% of his bloodline, and so was Uncle Drake, so while they weren’t killing like their teammates, all the Peak Spirit Emperors were on them.
Kaizo was surrounded by five Peak Spirit Emperors, and so was Uncle Drake, but despite being overpowered, they kept getting back up.
Since the enemy wasn’t about to ignore them and focus on the others, they weren’t having it easy at all.
The Seven Sea Kings held back Uncle Drake because he fought them at 10% of his power.
Anything higher, and he would have killed thousands, which would have included his own teammates.
However, things were different now.
The battlefield was open on all sides, and Uncle Drake could see only Forsaken warriors.
This made him start to fight more destructively, like a dragon should.
The enemy knew the damage he could cause, so they were going all out to stop him.
"How much higher can you go, Uncle Drake?" Kaizo asked, taking a sword swing with his hand, which was coated in a red metallic gauntlet.
"I can go as high as fifteen, but that will drain me rapidly.
However, just five is already good enough to hold these idiots back."
Kaizo laughed, landing a kick in a Forsaken warrior’s gut.
"I know, right?
They are much weaker than I expected."
"Very weak.
If I were to go up to seven, I am confident I can crush one’s head like a tomato."
"Why don’t you do it, Uncle Drake?"
"Are you sure?"
"I am.
I want to see a head pop."
"Very well."
Uncle Drake rose into the air, causing the Forsaken warriors to sense something was amiss, so they flew toward him, aiming to stop the annoying dragon at all costs.
"Idiots," Kaizo muttered coldly.
Then the heavens churned, and the clouds turned red and black.
From the clouds, a large black dragon moved, sending down a powerful pressure.
"Yi Lai, now."
The moment Kaizo spoke, Kent’s Dragon Necromancer appeared with her sword raised.
"Forbidden Art," she spoke in a sinister tone, causing the clouds to churn and thunder to rumble across the sky.
The Peak Spirit Emperors who chased after Uncle Drake turned and looked at Yi Lai, sensing something very bad was about to happen.

"It is rude to turn your back on your enemy." Uncle Drake, now in his human form, appeared behind one of the Spirit Emperors and grabbed his head, sinking his claws through his forehead and around his skull.
’Pop!’
With a pop, the Spirit Lord’s head was crushed like a tomato.
At the same time, Yi Lai was also ready...
"First Form: Domain Sealing Strike."
"Nooooo..."

chapters.title: Chapter 908: The Apocalypse (12)
paragraphs: "No!"
A Spirit Emperor shouted just as Yi Lai unleashed the sword attack.
A brilliant light burst from the strike, slamming into the red door with a powerful boom.
The door shuddered, and then the red light inside suddenly turned dark and shifted to green the next second...
Hundreds of forsaken warriors passing through the door froze when the attack landed. Then, in a quick flash, their bodies disintegrated into puddles of blood that flew toward Sylara.
"What have you done?" The Spirit Emperor, who shouted, charged toward Yi Lai with the intent to cut her head off her body.
However, before she could get close, a massive and deadly flaming hammer came out of nowhere and slammed into the forsaken warrior’s body, sending her crashing down.

"Thank you for the assist, Elyndra." Aetheris, the Flame Giant, appeared, standing twelve feet tall. He had suppressed his height to twelve feet, allowing him to wield his war hammer with a handle fourteen feet long.

Aetheris didn’t even turn to the Spirit Emperor, who was sent crashing by his colossal and deadly hammer. He knew there was no coming back from that, so he turned to the next Spirit Emperor with an evil grin on his cracked and molten lava face.
"What a refreshing battle," Aetheris muttered, moving like a living mountain. In the next second, his hammer came down hard, turning many Spirit Emperors and those below to meat paste.

"Kaizo, we have thirty minutes before the seal loses its power. Afterward, I can’t seal it again." Yi Lai flew toward Kaizo, but before she could get any closer, a spear came from an unknown direction.

She twisted mid-air and swung her sword backward, meeting the attack. Her body was pushed back several steps in the air. However, she merely snorted when her eyes landed on the forsaken warrior who attacked her.
"He is all yours, Nethar."
Before the Peak Spirit Emperor could make another move, a red dragon appeared through the void and swallowed him.
"Punk," Yi Lai muttered before turning back to Kaizo. "I will be leaving now to recover."
"You can go, Yi Lai. We will manage now that you’ve bought us some time," Kaizo replied. With no immediate danger around her, she was able to enter the tower.
The sword technique that she had used was too damaging to her body, so she needed to recover. Thankfully, Vexthra possesses the ability to heal her and the others much faster while inside the tower.
After all, an hour on the battlefield was a day inside the tower, and with Vexthra’s help, she would be away for only a few minutes.
But with her work accomplished, Kaizo’s plan—discussed with his team before the battle—entered phase two.
"Lani, time for you to remove some tattoos."
When Lani heard Kaizo’s words, she came to a stop. Vari, who was in the same location as her, also stopped and turned to Lani.
"Don’t worry, I’ll be around to make sure you don’t go too far."
Lani nodded and sighed.
Then she activated the forbidden skill she had recently unlocked.
Back when they were training with the Foxkin warriors in Fedora, she had gained an enlightenment that had something to do with the hundreds of millions of names tattooed on her body.
These tattoos appeared when Kent invoked her True Name. She had been trying to understand what they meant for months now, but she made no progress until the enlightenment a few weeks ago.
It turned out the names tattooed on her body were people she had unjustly killed in her previous life. These people didn’t deserve to die, but they fell to her dagger.
So even though she did something good in the end—which earned her a True Name—karma followed her into this new life.
Now, the millions of tattoos on her body were restrictions limiting her potential.
Her true potential, which she hadn’t realised just yet, was bound by every last tattoo on her body.
Of course, while that wasn’t too bad, considering she was now a powerhouse in her own right, these restrictions would soon begin revealing themselves as her cultivation base continued to increase.
However, this karma did not follow her into her new life without a way to break free.
The enlightenment revealed that for every bad person she killed, a tattoo would vanish, and she would regain a piece of her potential.
However, in order to do that, she had to enter a strange, frenzied state where her strength would increase tenfold.
Aside from the increase, every kill would reward her with a bloodlust that, if she had more than enough, she might lose control over.
So while gaining a 1000% boost in strength, which would allow her to kill like the Angel of Death, Lani didn’t want to lose control; thus, she was hesitant to activate it.
But she couldn’t hesitate now—not when her sisters and friends were being injured with every passing second.
Lani sighed again and activated the skill, ’Dance of the Endless Night.’

Her hair shortened, and her body became surrounded by shadows, raising her aura to an all-time high. The scythe in her hand elongated, and the sharp end of the blade was now coated by a deadly, deep red energy.
Tattoos appeared on every part of her body, some even appearing within her eyes.
"Time to pay for my sins."
With that, she moved, and what followed was a massacre so brutal that even Neomi, the Mother of Killers, raised her brow.
"It is not your turn, Neomi, so focus on delivering justice as Rakshasa," Kaizo said. Despite being surrounded by four Spirit Emperors, he was still paying attention to everyone on the battlefield.
Neomi smiled and continued to kill, something she was born to do.
On the other side of the door, the moment Yi Lai’s attack struck, the ten Heaven Ascension Stage warriors sensed the danger, forcing them to rush toward the gateway leading to Sonox.
However, they were a step too late.
By the time they arrived at the door, it had turned from red to green, sealing itself.
One of them formed a seal and pointed it at the door. A yellow gas flew from his finger, and when it landed on the door, he frowned.
"It has been sealed from the other side. However, it will open in half an hour."
"What? But how were they able to do something like that? Aren’t they merely Medium World nobodies? Or did Amix lie to us?"

"She didn’t lie. However, if she failed to tell us how powerful this world truly is, then it means they hid their strength very well," Deva, Amix’s supposed mother, who was also the Forsaken Queen, said, an uneasiness washing down her back.

"Right now, 250,000 warriors are dying on the other side of the door. Luckily, most are merely Spirit Ascensions. However, if this world is indeed as dangerous as it seems, the moment the door opens, five of you should lead the rest of the warriors and attack.
The rest of us will stay and welcome the Lord."
They nodded and began to wait. Deva and four of the Forsaken elders returned to the large building to wait for this mysterious Lord.
"Be ready, everyone. The moment the door is unsealed, we attack."
Over 200,000 warriors responded in unison.
In the meantime, while the forsaken race was blocked from sending reinforcement, Kaizo’s team was making headway.

chapters.title: Chapter 909: The Apocalypse (13)
paragraphs: "Damn it! Just where did these bastards come from?" The Pill Princess cursed, narrowly leaping away from a spear thrust launched by a Spirit Emperor.
Her forehead was drenched in sweat, showing she was at her limit.
Beside her, Princess Elowen released an arrow that let out a glass-shattering sound. The arrow pierced the shoulder of a Spirit Ascension Stage forsaken warrior.
The moment it struck, the warrior’s shoulder began to crystallize into glass. The corruption spread quickly down his arm, and before long, half his body had turned to glass.
He collapsed, shattering into cold ice. However, these chunks of ice were actually cold flames.
Princess Elowen turned to her left and saw her friend, Princess Freya of the dwarven race, slash her short sword at the leg of a Spirit Emperor.
She then swiftly moved aside, giving the Arrogant Crystal Dragon Prince the opening to unleash his crystal flame on the Spirit Emperor, searing his face and chest.

The One-Eyed Demon Spawn—renowned for his lightning-fast attacks and deadly swordplay—flashed across the battlefield. He struck with unmatched precision, severing the Spirit Emperor’s head before he could recover from the burning sensation on his face and chest.
Their coordination was seamless, just like how the Ice Maiden, Nyss, and the Venom King were working together, cutting down enemies as fast as they could.
In this very moment, aside from the Sect Elders, only the five seeded core disciples, Princess Elowen, Princess Freya, and Nyss, remained fighting on the battlefield.
Almost all other disciples had retreated to Sonox, with none daring to return.

Of course, away from the main battle yet still within the Dead Region, many of the disciples who had received Kent’s generosity lingered, stepping in only to support injured warriors or finish off wounded forsaken warriors that strayed within four hundred meters of their position.
However, to fully join the fray and seek out their own targets was something they dared not risk.
But because of their retreat, Alina’s use of her spiritual qi to maintain the formation was reduced. This allowed her to preserve hundreds more lives.
Even so, countless warriors continued to die, and there was nothing more she could do.

"I know Lady Enzi is famed for her battlefield presence, but who would have thought Lady Liora was this deadly?" the Ice Maiden said, briefly pausing as her eyes followed the dark-armored lady wielding two daggers, moving like a phantom through thousands of overpowered foes.
Initially, everyone had expected Lady Enzi alone to dominate the battlefield. However, that assumption crumbled when Lady Liora’s white robes abruptly shifted into dark leather armor.
Her long, silky brown hair darkened to jet black and was bound in a tight ponytail. In her grip gleamed two daggers, each brimming with death qi.
Naturally, she seized the spotlight, outshining both Lady Enzi and Sect Leader Deimos.
"She’s like the incarnation of a death sister," Nyss said, cutting into the ankle of a forsaken warrior and leaving the rest for her brother to finish.

"I suppose one cannot judge a book by its cover," remarked an elder fighting near the disciples. He thrust forward with his spear while bracing his shield, giving another elder the opening to deliver a lethal strike.
The Pill Princess, who had always seen her master as harmless and gentle, now stared in shock at the woman’s deadly precision as she tore through enemy ranks.
"Just who are you, Master?" she whispered.

On her arm, the red, brown, and white flame runes continued to absorb the soul essence of her kills. Perhaps because she was slaying beings whose cultivation bases far exceeded her own, each kill granted her even greater returns.
Yet the more she watched her master kill, the more she began to wonder if the woman she thought she knew had ever truly existed.
But with monstrous enemies pressing in on all sides, she was forced to bury her doubts and focus on survival.
As for Lady Enzi, watching her friend dominate the battlefield only fueled her hunger for strength.
’Kent is right. I’m still not strong enough. I must be able to kill even four realms above me before ascending.’
She threw her sword into the air and formed a seal, summoning nine identical blades that shot outward, striking nine forsaken warriors in unison.
"Once this is done, I will go into a one-year seclusion inside Kent’s tower and come out only after breaking three more limits and reforming my foundation.
My Glass Realm is stronger than ever, but my foundation is still lacking."
She moved, and the sound of glass shattering followed her steps. Within a ten-meter radius, every forsaken warrior who entered was immediately blinded by their own reflections.
So, while her cultivation was weaker, she was by no means weak.

The rules of cultivation were strange. It was even said that a careless god could fall to the sword of a mortal. So, although the forsaken warriors were far stronger than Sonox’s army, the battle wasn’t entirely pressing down on them.
Of course, some disciples and warriors died, but that was simply the price one must pay in war. Not all could survive the chaos of battle.

Lady Liora, the Silent Angel, glided through the fray of Spirit Ascensions and Spirit Emperors, killing those she was certain she could defeat and crippling those she could not, leaving them for Lady Enzi to finish off.
Back in her world, she was regarded as the disciple of a Pill Legend. Her fame stretched far and wide, even reaching the Supreme High Worlds.
In fact, she had once been invited by Five Pill Worlds to join their alliance, but she politely turned their offers down.
When her master ascended, she knew it was her turn to find a disciple and continue the ritual. Naturally, she longed to escape the burden of being the disciple of a Pill Legend.
But what no one knew was that, before becoming the disciple of the Pill Legend, she was a deadly assassin who had assassinated thousands.
The codename ’Silent Angel’ echoed through thousands of worlds, to the point that even the infamous Midnight Shadows sought her out.
When they discovered what drove her to kill, they extended their invitation—and she accepted.
Though she later became an alchemist, in her heart she remained an assassin.
This was why, when a righteous mission called, she chose to answer, even if her journey as an alchemist would be delayed for another thousand years.

"For the Faceless Assassin, I must kill all who dare harm the innocent." With that unshakable resolve in her heart, she moved like death itself, ignoring the strength gap between her and the forsaken warriors.
Unbeknownst to her, a yin-yang circle began to form on her forehead, and her eyes slowly darkened.
If one looked closely, they would see the yin—the dark half of the circle—overpowering the yang, the white half.
