chapters.title: Chapter 919: I Eat Immortals For Breakfast (3)
paragraphs: "Big sister, what is wrong?" Nara asked, looking at the pale expression on Vexthra’s face.
Hearing her question, Vexthra realised she had reacted in ways she shouldn’t have. But knowing it was already too late to take it back, she sighed and pointed at the screen.
"Watch first..."
On the battlefield, Kent tapped Lord Forsaken’s shoulder and injected blue Nirvana flames directly into his core.
The blue flame evaded his core instantly. The moment it did, Lord Forsaken froze in place, his face pale.
Kent deactivated his flame veins, feeling his energy draining at a rapid pace. However, his hand held the man in place. With the flame inside his core, he wouldn’t dare make any sudden movements.
"Well, looks who is about to die," Kent laughed, using his alchemy knowledge to swirl the flames inside Lord Forsaken’s core.
"You wouldn’t dare, mortal," Lord Forsaken said, shaking in his legs like a baby. His entire body was soaked in sweat as he was held under Kent’s firm grip.
To sweat that much within mere seconds shows he was in the highest level of panic.

"I dare do anything I want. Like I said earlier, the Forsaken race and I are now enemies, and until one of us is dead, there will never be peace between us. So before I send you packing, remember these words... Your bane of existence has awakened, and he is coming with blood and carnage."
"I am an immortal. You do not want to become my enemy." Lord Forsaken threatened, but Kent wasn’t afraid.
Kent sneered and gave a killer response, "I eat immortals for breakfast."
More flames surged into Lord Forsaken’s core before Kent shouted, "Explode."
"NOOOOOOO—"
His no was cut short since his core exploded the next second.
’Tower, I suppose we wouldn’t know the answer unless we see the real body. However, I believe we have sent him away the best way I could.’
⟦The master has indeed surpassed all expectations.⟧
"Thank you for your kind words, Tower." Kent smiled and looked toward Uncle Drake.
"What do you think? Did I let him off too easily?"
Uncle Drake could only smile at Kent as he flew toward him.
Meanwhile, inside the tower, Vexthra sighed inwardly and waved her hand, causing the screen displaying the battlefield to vanish.
She turned to her sisters and let out another sigh. She knew she had to explain to them what had just happened.
"In the world of cultivators, there are three things that are extremely important. They are the soul, body, and core.
All three of these things work hand in hand to keep the cultivator going.
However, in most cases, many can live without their body or even their soul. There are techniques out there that can keep the body going without the soul.
Or in the case of those who venture into the underworld to comprehend the laws, they can live without their bodies.

However, in either case, one cannot live without their core. Whether their bodies are moving without their soul or their souls are living without the body, they each have one thing in common, and that is the core.
So what do you think will happen if the core is injured?"

The ladies started to connect the dots, which immediately caused them to start turning pale. They could already see where Vexthra was going, and that was more than enough to tell them the severity of what had just happened to the immortal.
"Unlike clones, Avatars have something called mirror cores. This mirror core is a literal reflection of the main core inside the true body.
It is how the main body communicates with the Avatar, regardless of the distance between them. In a way, the two are linked by a thread that cannot be severed.
Of course, in the event that this thread is severed, the main body will only sustain some injuries that can be healed in a few years.
However, if someone uses that thread to gain access to the main core, the situation becomes much more dangerous.
What Kent did just now was inject his Nirvana flames into the mirror core, and using the thread, he touched the main core.
However, he went further and exploded the mirror core, which, in this case, since it was connected to the main core and had already been touched by him, the explosion affected the main core.
The chance of that immortal dying is high, but if he had acted faster when he sensed the presence of the flame, then he would be seriously injured by now." Vexthra let out a deep sigh.
Even as a literal god, what Kent did just now scared her.
"Though he nearly killed Val, what Kent did to him is several times more evil." Vexthra shook her head and sighed again.
[Planet Chacarro - A Forsaken Immortal World - Twenty seconds before the explosion]
Inside a tall, dark tower, a man with dark, twisted hair and delicate features sat in a lotus posture. His expression was twisted even more hideously than his hair.
Compared to his avatar, currently throwing swords at Kent, this look is much more terrifying.
Naturally, he was paying attention to something very important. If one looked closely, he had the aura of a Core Immortal. That was two stages above the one fighting Kent.
"Just die already," he muttered, yet those words shook the tower, causing many inside or around it to tremble, some coughing blood.
At that moment, on the battlefield in the Dead Region, ten thousand swords were raining down on Kent. He was sure this battle would end with his victory.
But that feeling washed away when Kent’s movement suddenly surged and kept surging until a sudden sound entered his ears, and Kent vanished from sight.
Before he could feel the wind, a dangerous feeling entered his core.
"NO!"
His voice was hoarse. However, before he could attempt to sever the connection between himself and the Avatar, the Nirvana flames entered his main core.
"NO!"
All the immortal qi in his body moved toward his core in an attempt to prevent the flames. However, Kent was a step ahead. He exploded his core, and the impact was immediate.
"NOOOOOO!"

His painful cry, which contained all his energy, flattened the tower and sent ripples spreading several miles. In an instant, all those below the rank of Life Stage and within the twelve-mile radius of the tower exploded.
Even those within or above the Life Stage sustained painful backlashes, with many passing out. Some lost their cultivation due to the sudden interruption.
In an instant, the entire planet felt like it had been struck by a large meteor.
Seven people appeared through the void the next second after the tower exploded. They each had a cultivation base of True Immortals, a stage above Lord Forsaken’s true cultivation.
"What happened?" one of them asked, looking at the tower now in ruins. Not even the foundation remained intact.
From the wreckage, a boulder moved, and the main body of Lord Forsaken was revealed.
His face was deadly pale.
"Bram, your cultivation... What happened?"

Lord Forsaken, whose true name was Bram, had now dropped from Core Immortal to the Peak of the Heavenly Ascension Stage. That was five stages wiped out by a brat who was only at the Core Formation Stage and hadn’t even refined his core yet.
"I want his head!" Bram shouted, his expression dark and ugly.
"Whose head?"
"I want his head!"
It would take Bram a couple of weeks to calm down, and then he would report what happened to his leaders. From there, a hunt for Kent would begin.
However, since nobody knew his name, looking for him would be next to impossible.
Without Kent even knowing, the Forsaken Race, who had been low-key for years, began to stir—and this time, they would be coming for his head.

chapters.title: Chapter 920: The Sea Race Fate
paragraphs: The battle came to an end the moment Lord Forsaken exploded.
Naturally, only Uncle witnessed that.
On the otherside of the crack, since nobody came out two hours after everyone else retreated, they began to sense that something had changed.
Of course, their guard only lowered when, three hours after they retreated, two people came out of the crack.
"Kent" Nyss was the first person to approach Kent the moment he walked out of the crack with Uncle Drake.
She was among the disciples who had retreated earlier. Aside from a few broken bones and cuts, she appeared to be fine.
Kent looked at her and smiled. "You’ve become much stronger since the last time we met." Kent held her hand and led her toward the various kings and the Sect elders.
"Sorry for being late. I was caught up in something I couldn’t escape from," Kent said when he approached them. They looked at him and sighed.
"It isn’t your fault. After all, had it not been for your people coming, Sonox would have long since fallen to the vampires or even the Sea Race," Sect Leader Deimos said, and the rest nodded.
"The fact that you came when we really needed saving is already enough," Queen Jascia also said, though she wasn’t in the right body to be active.

Just like Sect Leader Deimos, she and most of the leaders had burned their life force for the battle, so they were very tired. The only reason they were even awake now was to ensure that everything was indeed over first.

Kent looked at their faces and smiled. He pointed his finger upward, and a formation appeared. Then, from the formation, Spirit Grape Fruits started flying out, landing in the palm of every warrior around.
Even the injured and unconscious ones received one. The vampires were the same. Now that they were all under Asha’s control, they wouldn’t be able to rebel even if they wanted to.
Naturally, shocked expressions spread across everyone’s faces when they received these fruits.
"It will help with your fatigue and speed up your healing. After that, you can all go back to the Dead Region and collect the bodies of the fallen."
Their faces sank when they heard Kent’s words.
It was a battle, and they knew people were bound to die. However, the odds they went against weren’t ones they had seen coming.
So, in a way, the deaths were several times more painful than they should have been if it had been a fair battle.
"It was a battle to protect your world and loved ones. Those who fell believed in that resolve, and that was why they fought with all they had.
The best we can do now is ensure there won’t be a next time, that their sacrifice won’t be in vain." They lightened up a bit.

"I will send packages to your various kingdoms and states. All of you will receive some, so when you do, use them well to strengthen yourselves. Though the Forsaken Race won’t be coming back again, there is no telling who might appear next time.
So let’s prepare and make sure that next time, not even a single one of you will fall in combat." They nodded, but one wounded half-elf raised his hand to ask a question.
Kent, of course, allowed him to ask.

"What about the Sea Race? Are we just going to let them go scot-free?" The look on this half-elf’s face showed he was very angry. And he should be. His best friend had fallen victim to an attack from a Sea Beast.
It wasn’t just him who had that question in mind. Several others wore angry looks on their faces.
Kent just smiled and pointed to the vampires. "Just like what happened to these vampires, the same thing awaits them." Kent flew into the air and amplified his voice.
"I declare that from today onwards, the Vampire Race and the Sea Beasts will become guardians of Sonox.
Your various leaders will receive tokens that will allow them to command them when the need arises." Kent looked around and saw that most weren’t happy about his declaration, so he chose to clarify.

"Killing them will be a waste. Of course, if there are necromancers among you, it would be a bountiful harvest. However, none of you can raise the dead, so why kill them when we can make them servants for good?
I personally despise slavery, so we won’t be turning them into mindless drones. However, we also won’t be allowing them to attack this world ever again."
Kent snapped his finger, and Alina appeared. "This is Alina, my beautiful wife. She is a Formation/Array King. You can just call her the Rune King if you wish.

She has already started working on a formation that will forever make the Sea Beasts guardians of this world. Rest assured, they will forever continue to serve for generations to come, until all kingdoms and states in this world deem it enough to free them.
They went against the world, which housed them and fed them, and thus, their punishment will be passed down for generations to come."
This time, after listening to his reasoning, they calmed down a little. It would take them a while to fully process the situation, but soon they would come to terms with this new arrangement.
Soon, everyone went back to their various kingdoms. The sect also left, leaving only Lady Liora and Enzi. One of them wanted to speak with Kent, and the other wanted to speak with Vari.
In the end, Kent took them into the tower, causing Lady Liora to widen her eyes when they arrived in the Body Tower.
Kent asked his wives to meet them there since he had no plans of sending them to the Harem Tower just yet.
Val was already awake, but the damage dealt to her body was far more severe, so she chose to fully heal inside the Yin Pool before coming out.
Kent only stood at a distance to examine her before leaving.
He would reward her when she was done healing.
A week has passed since the battle. Life hadn’t returned to normal yet, but thanks to Kent’s generosity spreading far and wide, everyone had begun to adapt.
Kent returned to the sect with Lady Enzi, while Lady Liora stayed in the tower to fully work on her partially balanced Yin-Yang Death Circle. Vari, of course, was helping her with that.

Kent had some matters to handle before the interplanetary competition in two weeks. The sect informed the alliance of what had happened, requesting an extension of the date, but the request was rejected.
Naturally, it was unreasonable that the offer was turned down, considering many had died, including disciples and sect elders.
However, even though the request was denied, the disciples didn’t mind. After fighting against Spirit Kings and the like, they were more than ready to face the competition with deadly precision.
Kent also made sure they were prepared.
However, before that, Kent had to attend to his own business. After all, he had quests to review and his gains to examine after his Blood Enlightenment.
Aside from that, he had memory keys waiting to be used to unlock more memories of his past lives.
He entered a two-week seclusion, which was the equivalent of over 300 days for him inside the tower.

chapters.title: Chapter 921: Amix’s Fate
paragraphs: Inside a dark room, where the high-pitched squeaks, clicks, and chirps of bats could be heard, lay a beautiful lady chained with special bindings imbued with lightning.
Her wrists were bound in a rather soft substance, preventing them from bleeding or turning red. Perhaps her jailors weren’t entirely cruel.
However, if one looked closely, they would see a faintly glowing purple runic mark on her forehead.
The same mark appeared on Kent’s forehead as he walked into the Tower Prison.
He was done with matters outside, and with two weeks remaining before the sect competition, which he planned to participate in this time, he intended to deal with some of his tasks first.
The first task, of course, was to interrogate Amix, the once-leader of the Hand.
Kent didn’t believe for one second that she was innocent, nor that she had simply been brainwashed into doing what she did.
Colluding with the Forsaken Race was a crime punishable by death to the last descendant. She had sinned gravely. However, she wasn’t entirely consumed by darkness, nor beyond redemption.
In truth, she had been manipulated by Deva into committing those crimes. Of course, she wasn’t the only one, so Kent wanted to learn about the others by first learning about Amix.
The purple rune was merely a truth detector given to him by Alina. Little did she know, Kent could delve into Amix’s mind and extract whatever he wished.
"You look cosy," Kent said as he appeared before Amix’s cell.
The once dignified leader of the Hand, now in chains, raised her head and glared at him. Her eyes were filled with anger.
Kent simply smiled at her expression.
"Since this happens to be our first meeting, what do you say we have a nice discussion? I happen to be in a good mood today, so why don’t we keep it that way?"
The anger in Amix’s eyes deepened. "Just kill me, because I will not tell you anything."
Kent laughed, retrieved a chair from his space ring, and sat down. "Who said I came here to fish for information? I merely came to have a nice discussion."
Amix remained motionless, but Kent didn’t mind. In fact, he found satisfaction in the defiance written on her face.
"I will speak, and you would do well to listen." Kent truly just came to have a nice discussion.
"When I first learned that you were the one who opened the Forsaken Door, my very first thought was to sever your head from your body.

However, after sitting down to think about it, I realised killing you would be an act of mercy. After all, your rebellion was crushed, wiped from the face of the universe. Every last hope you had of becoming some princess in the Forsaken Race vanished along with them.
Your precious Hand was obliterated, and every last fang of your organisation was killed in the most agonising way possible.
So, essentially, you lost everything. That means killing you would actually be the kindest fate you could hope for."

"This is why I won’t be killing you today, nor ever. Instead, two doors now open before you. By the end of this discussion, one will slam shut in your face, and the other will close firmly behind you.
So why don’t you relax your heart and listen? Trust me, you wouldn’t want to miss a single word."
Kent laughed, but his laughter lacked friendliness.
"First, I recently received a rather unique ability that requires a human or a beast to cultivate. Now, I don’t want to sound like that evil cultivator whom everyone fears.
However, whatever thought came to your mind at this moment is indeed right on point. I plan on turning you into a living furnace to cultivate a seal which I know will hurt like hell.
It won’t kill you, but you will wish it would. That is my first offer, and it is for you to become my furnace to cultivate a technique"
Amix, who was already pale, turned even whiter. But Kent’s eyes showed no sympathy.
"Second, a subordinate of mine has just discovered a way to turn the living into half-dead. You will accept her offer and become half-dead, which means you will partially become half-undead.
When that ends, you will be sent to a world where you will undergo a life-or-death trial. If you pass, your life will be spared. If you fail, your life will end in the most agonising way possible."
Kent stood up. "You can think of your answer and let me know whenever you are ready."

With that, Kent vanished from the prison, leaving behind a panting Amix whose face was dark with both anger and fear. The offer Kent gave her was something she would never want to go through—especially the first one.

The second, however, was shrouded in uncertainty. She didn’t know what the trial Kent spoke of would be like, but she knew that anything other than being killed outright was already a fate worse than death.
Kent left and returned to the Sword Tower.
It was only after he sat down that a smile appeared on his face.
"Though the first offer was a lie, the second will give Yi Lai exactly what she wanted."

Yi Lai had received an ability that allows her to send ordinary people to a dragon world called Abyssmy. Though its name is funny, it is a place where all who appear there would undergo a dragon trial, and if they passed, they would become dragons.

Yi Lai, who could only turn dragons into her undead, knew this was her chance to expand her army. She would turn Amix into a half-undead, and then, after Amix passed the trial, she would become a full undead dragon under Yi Lai’s control.
However, if Amix failed, being half-undead meant she wouldn’t die even if the dragons tore her apart. And living in a world filled with rogue dragons wasn’t exactly ideal.
Yi Lai had warned her that if she failed the trial, she would suffer unimaginable pain. So with that fear instilled in her, she will work harder to pass.
After all, the only reason she is still alive is due to her unique constitution and the prospect of what she will become in the future.
Kent then began tallying everything he had left to handle before ascending.
"I now have four memory keys for Chaos and Jest. As for Faceless, I only have three more to go. If I manage to review all three memories, I’m sure my combat power will take a huge leap.
Aside from that, I also have to review my new cultivation method and the gifts from my Blood Enlightenment. I need to handle those carefully.
Then I must become a Sword Sage and, if possible, a Sword King.
Then there’s the matter of becoming a Pill Saint—or even a Pill Sage.
Luckily for me, I know exactly where to go to achieve my first breakthroughs. But gaining nine more enlightenments on the sword path will be a true headache."

Kent scratched the back of his head. The workload remaining to be handled was overwhelming. Though he had already become undisputed even against a Heavenly Ascension stage expert, Kent knew that true dominance was not yet his.
He had yet to face a Heavenly Ascension stage expert from a Supreme High World. Naturally, the reason he wanted to reach all these stages was thanks to what he saw during his Blood Enlightenment.
He knew where he had to go after he ascended, and knowing that, he realised he had to grow much stronger before he could ascend.
"That’s it. I must become a Sword King, a Pill King, form 10,000-plus Flame Veins, and forge the first Blood Core Gate before ascending. This means I must visit the past more often.
Additionally, there is the issue of the Life Blood Seal and the Death Blood Seal I acquired through my enlightenment.
But first, I have to handle these memories."
Kent took out a memory key and activated it, flooding his mind with memories directly.

sentences.text: Inside a dark room, where the high-pitched squeaks, clicks, and chirps of bats could be heard, lay a beautiful lady chained with special bindings imbued with lightning.
Her wrists were bound in a rather soft substance, preventing them from bleeding or turning red.
Perhaps her jailors weren’t entirely cruel.
However, if one looked closely, they would see a faintly glowing purple runic mark on her forehead.
The same mark appeared on Kent’s forehead as he walked into the Tower Prison.
He was done with matters outside, and with two weeks remaining before the sect competition, which he planned to participate in this time, he intended to deal with some of his tasks first.
The first task, of course, was to interrogate Amix, the once-leader of the Hand.
Kent didn’t believe for one second that she was innocent, nor that she had simply been brainwashed into doing what she did.
Colluding with the Forsaken Race was a crime punishable by death to the last descendant.
She had sinned gravely.
However, she wasn’t entirely consumed by darkness, nor beyond redemption.
In truth, she had been manipulated by Deva into committing those crimes.
Of course, she wasn’t the only one, so Kent wanted to learn about the others by first learning about Amix.
The purple rune was merely a truth detector given to him by Alina.
Little did she know, Kent could delve into Amix’s mind and extract whatever he wished.
"You look cosy," Kent said as he appeared before Amix’s cell.
The once dignified leader of the Hand, now in chains, raised her head and glared at him.
Her eyes were filled with anger.
Kent simply smiled at her expression.
"Since this happens to be our first meeting, what do you say we have a nice discussion?
I happen to be in a good mood today, so why don’t we keep it that way?"
The anger in Amix’s eyes deepened.
"Just kill me, because I will not tell you anything."
Kent laughed, retrieved a chair from his space ring, and sat down.
"Who said I came here to fish for information?
I merely came to have a nice discussion."
Amix remained motionless, but Kent didn’t mind.
In fact, he found satisfaction in the defiance written on her face.
"I will speak, and you would do well to listen." Kent truly just came to have a nice discussion.
"When I first learned that you were the one who opened the Forsaken Door, my very first thought was to sever your head from your body.
However, after sitting down to think about it, I realised killing you would be an act of mercy.
After all, your rebellion was crushed, wiped from the face of the universe.
Every last hope you had of becoming some princess in the Forsaken Race vanished along with them.
Your precious Hand was obliterated, and every last fang of your organisation was killed in the most agonising way possible.
So, essentially, you lost everything.
That means killing you would actually be the kindest fate you could hope for."
"This is why I won’t be killing you today, nor ever.
Instead, two doors now open before you.
By the end of this discussion, one will slam shut in your face, and the other will close firmly behind you.
So why don’t you relax your heart and listen?
Trust me, you wouldn’t want to miss a single word."
Kent laughed, but his laughter lacked friendliness.
"First, I recently received a rather unique ability that requires a human or a beast to cultivate.
Now, I don’t want to sound like that evil cultivator whom everyone fears.
However, whatever thought came to your mind at this moment is indeed right on point.
I plan on turning you into a living furnace to cultivate a seal which I know will hurt like hell.
It won’t kill you, but you will wish it would.
That is my first offer, and it is for you to become my furnace to cultivate a technique"
Amix, who was already pale, turned even whiter.
But Kent’s eyes showed no sympathy.
"Second, a subordinate of mine has just discovered a way to turn the living into half-dead.
You will accept her offer and become half-dead, which means you will partially become half-undead.
When that ends, you will be sent to a world where you will undergo a life-or-death trial.
If you pass, your life will be spared.
If you fail, your life will end in the most agonising way possible."
Kent stood up.
"You can think of your answer and let me know whenever you are ready."
With that, Kent vanished from the prison, leaving behind a panting Amix whose face was dark with both anger and fear.
The offer Kent gave her was something she would never want to go through—especially the first one.
The second, however, was shrouded in uncertainty.
She didn’t know what the trial Kent spoke of would be like, but she knew that anything other than being killed outright was already a fate worse than death.
Kent left and returned to the Sword Tower.
It was only after he sat down that a smile appeared on his face.
"Though the first offer was a lie, the second will give Yi Lai exactly what she wanted."

She would turn Amix into a half-undead, and then, after Amix passed the trial, she would become a full undead dragon under Yi Lai’s control.
However, if Amix failed, being half-undead meant she wouldn’t die even if the dragons tore her apart.
And living in a world filled with rogue dragons wasn’t exactly ideal.
Yi Lai had warned her that if she failed the trial, she would suffer unimaginable pain.
So with that fear instilled in her, she will work harder to pass.

chapters.title: Chapter 922: Bloodline Strengthened
paragraphs: ⟦Congratulations, your bloodline has become stronger. Current Awakening: 18%⟧
⟦You can now harness 9% of your bloodline power⟧
A smile appeared on Kent’s face when this message appeared.
The first memory of the day was all about Chaos, his first incarnation, exploring the worlds outside his own with his new human friend, Elina.

After making sure everyone understood what he would do if anyone dared to touch his planet and people, none of the worlds in the planetary alliance wanted to come anywhere close to the Chaos world, Lumen.
Most of the memory showed how Chaos was slowly beginning to find the cultures of the worlds he was taken to by Elina fascinating. He was slowly coming to like humans, which was a huge win for him.
Kent shook his head slightly.

"I didn’t unlock any new bloodline aspect, but I am slowly inching closer to the 25% that will allow me to take on my full dragon form." A smile appeared on Kent’s face as he retrieved the second memory key and activated it.

His mind was yet again filled with so many memories that he had to take his time to sort them out. However, when he was done, Kent’s gaze turned cold, making him look away from the message that appeared before him.
"The Forsaken Race," he muttered.

The majority of the memories were still about Chaos exploring the human world with his only friend, Elina. Naturally, that was a happy memory, for without Chaos even knowing, Elina was slowly worming her way into his stone heart.
They had happy dates. Chaos had no idea what they meant. Naturally, Kent knew it wasn’t his fault. He knew Chaos grew up knowing only violence, so love was entirely new to him.
However, eventually, Elina was doing her best to make him aware of her feelings.
The last part of the memories was two years after Chaos left his world, Lumen. In the past two years, nothing had happened to it.

However, he received reports, or more accurately, Elina received reports, of a rogue race called the Forsaken Race. The report began by stating that this Forsaken Race was slowly making its way to the star system where Chaos and Elina’s worlds were located.
This prompted Chaos to leave and go back to his world, just in case his world was one of the many targets.
Naturally, this meant parting ways with Elina, who would also be needed to defend her world should things go badly.
"I have a bad feeling about this."
Kent first checked his progress, and aside from his bloodline becoming much stronger, there was no progress in the awakening part or in the amount he could harness in combat.
With that, Kent chose to check the third memory.
The moment he activated the key, his vision darkened.
[Memory Review - Chaos]
"I will be sure to send those Forsaken idiots packing and get back here so we can continue our travels," Chaos said to Elina, holding her hand.
They were seated on a roof made from the finest wood. Naturally, this was Elina’s world.
"I will wait for you, Chaos. And remember what I told you."
Chaos smiled. "I will be sure to let the people appoint new kings and queens to rule instead of leaving them in fear of my wrath every day."
Elina smiled, tiptoed, and gently kissed Chaos on the lips before running away with her cheeks red like a ripe tomato.
Chaos watched her leave with a blank expression. After she left, he chuckled and said, "Humans."
With that remark, he retrieved a small flying boat which could travel through the void. He made it float, and with that, he was gone.
It took a week, but he managed to get back to his world, which was surprisingly intact. The first thing he did was follow Elina’s advice and let the people select their leaders.

He became something akin to a planet protector, and in no time, life on Lumen started to blossom. The various beasts in the world began forming alliances and bonds that would remain strong for years to come.
Three months passed in the blink of an eye, but nothing happened.

"Are these Forsaken people afraid of this world or what? They should just come so I can slaughter them and go back to Elina, who promised to take me to a festival coming up in two and a half years’ time."

Chaos said this while hovering 2,000 miles outside planet Lumen. He had been staying there for the past three months, making sure that whatever danger found its way into his world would be dealt with before it even approached the planet.
However, even after nine more months, nothing happened.
This made Chaos wonder whether the report was genuine or not.
Naturally, he trusted Elina more than anything, so he knew she wouldn’t show him a fake report. Because of this trust, Chaos chose to remain outside the planet for another five months.
If nothing and nobody came, he would leave and head back to Elina’s world.
On this day, exactly three months into the five months he had set for himself, a large ship appeared thousands of miles away from his planet.
Naturally, Chaos became happy that those he had been waiting for all this time had finally arrived. He immediately started approaching them at a speed that could shatter mountains.
However, as he drew closer, he saw it wasn’t just one ship but dozens of them, causing him to slow down. Of course, he wasn’t about to cower in fear and run.
The reason he slowed down was that he recognised those ships. Naturally, his gaze was drawn to the poor state some of the ships were in when they came out of the void.
"Elina!" Chaos’s voice boomed, causing the thousands on the ship to freeze in place when they saw the demi-dragon speeding toward them like a meteor.
When he drew close, they all sighed in relief. However, Chaos wasn’t about to chit-chat with them.
"Where is Elina?" Chaos asked, but everyone’s face sank.
"Where is she?" This time, his voice shook everyone.
"She... she stayed behind," a middle-aged man said, his voice shaky and weak.

That was all Chaos needed to hear before he retrieved his boat and started flying through the void. It would take him a week to get to Elina’s world. However, Chaos wasn’t about to wait that long, so he pushed the flying boat to its limit.

Four days later, he emerged from the void 2,000 km away from Elina’s world. What he saw immediately made him shake his head in disbelief. With a mad dash, he appeared in a world where everything was in ruins before his eyes.
Millions had died, and the entire world was covered in smoke mixed with the pungent stench of blood and charred human remains.

"Elina!" Chaos called out as he flew toward her residence. Along the way, he realised Elina was in the army, so he changed direction and began flying toward the place where the strongest scent of blood was coming from.
It took him only a few seconds to arrive. However, when he saw the sight before him, he fell from the air and crashed to the ground.
"NOOOOOOOO..."
The entire tower shook as a primal aura—one filled with extreme hatred—enveloped everyone.

chapters.title: Chapter 923: Tyranny & Sorrow
paragraphs: "What is happening?" Tribe Chief Malthar asked, staring up at the sky above Blood City. It was now littered with cracks.
Behind him, thousands of Bloodveins stood, their faces pale with panic and fear.
This was their first time sensing danger after settling down in the Tower. In fact, the danger they sensed was even greater than when they were in the Dark Region.
This made them begin to panic.
Inside Gaiaville, too, the humans wore panicked expressions as they gazed at the cracks in the sky. In truth, the cracks were merely a horrifying sight.
The real danger was the air bearing down on them. It was filled with bloodlust and tyrannical heartbreak, something that made them both afraid and filled them with sorrow.
However, before any of them could despair, Vexthra appeared over the Tower City and amplified her voice, "Relax, everyone, there is no danger coming."
After saying that, she vanished and appeared inside the Sword Tower, where, aside from Kent, only Gaia was in sight.
Kent’s ladies could not come to the Sword Tower at the moment, as it was filled with Blood Qi, Sword Qi, and a few other auras that Kent himself did not even know he had.
If anyone aside from Vexthra were to appear there, they would be reduced to nothing by the terrifying auras in the air.
So the Tower prevented them from entering.
"What is happening to him?" Vexthra asked, looking at Kent seated in a lotus posture, a wave of red energy emitting from his eyes and red and dark symbols appearing on his face and all over his body.

Gaia held a panicked look in her eyes as she turned to Vexthra. "I don’t know what is happening to him, big sister. However, I knew he was retrieving his memories when, all of a sudden, this happened."
"Don’t you like to have access to his mind or something?" Vexthra asked. She, too, had a panicked expression in her eyes.
"No, big sister. I am not Dori, so I cannot access his mind."
Vexthra chewed her lips as frustration bubbled in her chest. "Isn’t there something I can do to help him?"
Gaia pondered for a moment and said, "I can send big sister into the master’s mind, but there will be a backlash even I cannot predict."
"I don’t care about backlashes. Even if it costs me my life, I will do it." Vexthra moved and landed two meters away from Kent.

Even with her divine aura coating her, she could sense the emotions bubbling in Kent’s eyes affecting her. However, she refused to focus on that just yet. The mission now was to stop Kent from destroying the Tower.
Gaia also moved and appeared beside Vexthra.
"Sit before him and press your forehead against his." Vexthra did as Gaia instructed.
"The moment I activate the fusion, you will enter the master’s mind. I do not know what will happen, but find him and bring him out."
Vexthra nodded and closed her eyes.
Gaia took a step back and formed a hand seal. Then she activated the Mind Fusion. Two golden symbols appeared on Vexthra’s and Kent’s foreheads. Then she felt her mind merge with Kent’s.
[Kent’s Mind - What Happened to Elina]
Vexthra appeared in a city in ruins. All around her, all she could see was death and fire. The destruction was just too much for even a goddess.
For a moment, she froze, unsure how to describe the horror surrounding her.
However, she recovered when her goddess side took over, making it almost as if the death of millions, including children, meant nothing to her.
Her focus then shifted to her main objective, which was to find Kent. She doesn’t know how long she can remain in this place, so she chooses to act fast.
Because she is a goddess, it was rather simple. Using her superior senses, she heard a sobbing sound a couple of miles away.
She moved in that direction, and in no time, she saw Kent on his knees, holding somebody in his arms.
Naturally, the figure before her wasn’t exactly Kent. It was Chaos, but with Kent’s consciousness.
"Kent," Vexthra called out. However, he neither turned nor acknowledged her. He only continued to sob as he clutched the person tightly in his arms.
Vexthra moved closer. It was after a few steps that she saw the person in Kent’s arms was a woman.
Her attention fell on Elina, lying lifeless in Kent’s embrace.

A smile lingered on her face, and a tiara rested upon her head. Although Vexthra was using her goddess nature, this sight broke her. Looking at the smile on Elina’s face, lying lifeless in Kent’s arms, punched a wound in her heart.
The tiara she wore has something about it.
One might even ask, why wear a tiara while clad in battle armour? It made no sense. Looking at her, drenched in her own blood and that of her enemies, the Tiara stood out.
But this tiara was something Chaos had bought for her during one of their many trips across the dozens of human worlds they had explored.
Back then, she had wanted dragon horns like Chaos. But since she was human, both she and Chaos knew she could only dream.
However, although Chaos had not realised how much it meant to her, he had bought her a golden tiara. And now, in her last moments, she had chosen to wear it, dying with a smile on her face.
Without realising it, Vexthra began to shed tears. She moved closer to Kent and hugged him from behind.
No words were spoken.
Just hugging him was all the words she needed to say. She was telling him she was there for him, and that alone was slowly melting Kent’s heart.
However, what the rest of the universe never knew was that this Elina, the one person who was the sole reason this universe still stood, had, in a way, found her way back into Kent’s life.
Had it not been for her death, Chaos would never have become who he was during the Primordial Era. It was only after she died that Chaos realised his true feelings for her.
He finally understood that all those annoying things Elina had made him do were part of her elaborate plan to make the stone-hearted Chaos fall in love with her.
And though she died, her efforts bore fruit. It was one of the many reasons Chaos never loved again, not even when the universe itself proposed to him.

To him, his stone heart had belonged to only one person during the Primordial Era. That person was Elina Hendrix Littlewolf—the weakest human Chaos had ever known, yet the one who became the source of his greatest strength.
A strength he once used to defy fate and rewrite the destiny of the universe.
A few hours later, Kent opened his eyes outside, while Vexthra fell back, unconscious, unsure when she would wake.
Kent briefly left seclusion to ensure she was safe before returning. He wasn’t in the right mindset to remain around anyone, not even his wives.
Meanwhile, on a faraway planet, controlled by a powerful family among the Supreme High Worlds, a young lady sat in chains with a slave collar around her neck, eating half-baked bread inside a cave.
She was one of the thousands enslaved inside what appeared to be a Spirit Crystal mine.
As she ate the bread, tears streamed slowly down her face.
She did not know why she was crying, but at that moment, all she could do was let the tears flow uncontrollably.

Even with her divine aura coating her, she could sense the emotions bubbling in Kent’s eyes affecting her.
However, she refused to focus on that just yet.
The mission now was to stop Kent from destroying the Tower.
Gaia also moved and appeared beside Vexthra.
"Sit before him and press your forehead against his." Vexthra did as Gaia instructed.
"The moment I activate the fusion, you will enter the master’s mind.
I do not know what will happen, but find him and bring him out."
Vexthra nodded and closed her eyes.
Gaia took a step back and formed a hand seal.
Then she activated the Mind Fusion.
Two golden symbols appeared on Vexthra’s and Kent’s foreheads.
Then she felt her mind merge with Kent’s.
[Kent’s Mind - What Happened to Elina]
Vexthra appeared in a city in ruins.
All around her, all she could see was death and fire.
The destruction was just too much for even a goddess.
For a moment, she froze, unsure how to describe the horror surrounding her.
However, she recovered when her goddess side took over, making it almost as if the death of millions, including children, meant nothing to her.
Her focus then shifted to her main objective, which was to find Kent.
She doesn’t know how long she can remain in this place, so she chooses to act fast.
Because she is a goddess, it was rather simple.
Using her superior senses, she heard a sobbing sound a couple of miles away.
She moved in that direction, and in no time, she saw Kent on his knees, holding somebody in his arms.
Naturally, the figure before her wasn’t exactly Kent.
It was Chaos, but with Kent’s consciousness.
"Kent," Vexthra called out.
However, he neither turned nor acknowledged her.
He only continued to sob as he clutched the person tightly in his arms.
Vexthra moved closer.
It was after a few steps that she saw the person in Kent’s arms was a woman.
Her attention fell on Elina, lying lifeless in Kent’s embrace.
A smile lingered on her face, and a tiara rested upon her head.
Although Vexthra was using her goddess nature, this sight broke her.
Looking at the smile on Elina’s face, lying lifeless in Kent’s arms, punched a wound in her heart.
The tiara she wore has something about it.
One might even ask, why wear a tiara while clad in battle armour?
It made no sense.
Looking at her, drenched in her own blood and that of her enemies, the Tiara stood out.
But this tiara was something Chaos had bought for her during one of their many trips across the dozens of human worlds they had explored.
Back then, she had wanted dragon horns like Chaos.
But since she was human, both she and Chaos knew she could only dream.
However, although Chaos had not realised how much it meant to her, he had bought her a golden tiara.
And now, in her last moments, she had chosen to wear it, dying with a smile on her face.
Without realising it, Vexthra began to shed tears.
She moved closer to Kent and hugged him from behind.
No words were spoken.
Just hugging him was all the words she needed to say.
She was telling him she was there for him, and that alone was slowly melting Kent’s heart.
However, what the rest of the universe never knew was that this Elina, the one person who was the sole reason this universe still stood, had, in a way, found her way back into Kent’s life.
Had it not been for her death, Chaos would never have become who he was during the Primordial Era.
It was only after she died that Chaos realised his true feelings for her.
He finally understood that all those annoying things Elina had made him do were part of her elaborate plan to make the stone-hearted Chaos fall in love with her.
And though she died, her efforts bore fruit.
It was one of the many reasons Chaos never loved again, not even when the universe itself proposed to him.
To him, his stone heart had belonged to only one person during the Primordial Era.
That person was Elina Hendrix Littlewolf—the weakest human Chaos had ever known, yet the one who became the source of his greatest strength.
A strength he once used to defy fate and rewrite the destiny of the universe.
A few hours later, Kent opened his eyes outside, while Vexthra fell back, unconscious, unsure when she would wake.
Kent briefly left seclusion to ensure she was safe before returning.
He wasn’t in the right mindset to remain around anyone, not even his wives.
Meanwhile, on a faraway planet, controlled by a powerful family among the Supreme High Worlds, a young lady sat in chains with a slave collar around her neck, eating half-baked bread inside a cave.
She was one of the thousands enslaved inside what appeared to be a Spirit Crystal mine.
As she ate the bread, tears streamed slowly down her face.
She did not know why she was crying, but at that moment, all she could do was let the tears flow uncontrollably.

chapters.title: Chapter 924: The Price Of Failure
paragraphs: "What happened to Big Sister?" Unity asked when Kent appeared inside the harem tower carrying Vexthra.

"She helped me with something and passed out after." Kent set her down on the bed. He used his finger to tenderly move the hair falling on the side of her face. "Don’t worry, she will be fine. She just needs to rest for a while."
He had already checked with the tower, and aside from Vexthra passing out due to exhaustion, nothing else seemed to be wrong with her.
However, as to when she will wake up, even the tower doesn’t know.
"Take care of her while I am away." The ladies nodded, and Kent vanished back to the sword tower. The moment he appeared, his eyes turned red as veins popped on his forehead.
The look of both regret and failure was evident on his face. But there was extreme hatred that seemed to be directed toward the forsaken race, burning wildly in his eyes.
"If I don’t eradicate every last one of you, then my name is not Kent."
Kent never expected the third memory to be so deeply ingrained in his being. It was overwhelming to the point that he would prefer it not happen ever again.
So far, he had experienced four ways he could review his past memories.
The first was, of course, taking a third-person seat and watching his memories unfold. He had experienced that with all three of his past lives.
The second, of course, was meeting his past selves. That one too happened when he was reviewing Chaos and Faceless’s memories.
Naturally, he knew this method would only happen once, unless, of course, he were to come across something that once belonged to him with his divine sense imbued in it.

The third was the diaries, which so far were Kent’s favourite, for he knew that after every diary, he would gain enlightenment. He had already gained four enlightenments for just his Chaos Dragon form.
However, he never expected the fourth method to be this drastic. This time, he was thrown into Chaos’s life, causing him to relive his memories.

Unlike the first method, this one made him feel whatever Chaos felt back then. So, while he couldn’t control how things unfolded, he was forced to relive the memories, and that alone was more than a person could bear, especially when they were not prepared.
Kent felt the love Elina had for him, and while the current him would have reciprocated that love, Chaos had been clueless until it was too late.

In that moment, when he saw the ships appear from the void, he knew what had happened. However, while he didn’t even know it, the love and feelings he never realised he had for Elina began to ignite, and that was what sent him flying to her world.
But the sight of Elina’s lifeless body was what broke him.
The fury he was going through at the moment was more than he had felt back then. In fact, back then, Chaos was only cultivating the Primal Body Tempering Art.
However, now, he was cultivating both the Primal Core Formation Diagram and the Primal Body Tempering Art.
Furthermore, after attaining the Blood Enlightenment, he acquired a unique yet perilous martial technique deeply rooted in bloodshed and slaughter.
It was safe to say he was now set to walk the path of slaughter.
This discovery had awakened the latent bloodlust inherent in his unique cultivation path. If he were to dive deeper, what Dori warned him about might happen.
He might just lose his mind and go on a slaughter spree.
Kent held the last memory key in his hand for three good hours before storing it back in his tower space.
"I need to hold back on that for now." He sighed. "In fact, I need to hold back on all the memories until Dori wakes up. Who is to say the next memory won’t get my blood boiling again?"
Kent sighed, knowing this trauma would take some time to heal. However, that didn’t mean he would slow down.
He might not be in the right mindset to be around his wives, which they understood, but that doesn’t mean he couldn’t handle other things.
He opened the system interface and saw that he had a substantial amount of Attribute Points. This meant he could break some more limits on his body.

"From the moment I became a Core Formation expert, the Yin Essence Vexthra sealed within my body started to show its use. If I were to follow the ordinary path and refine my core, I would have done so seven times already, reaching the peak.

However, with this path I have chosen, her yin-qi and the others cannot help with my cultivation, at least not when slaughter and bloodlust are considered" A smile appeared on Kent’s face despite the pain he was in.
"Of course, this is a good thing. Since their Yin Essence cannot help with my cultivation, it means all that power will be directed toward breaking the limits."
"I don’t know if this is a blessing or a curse, but if just one limit can double or even triple my strength, then who is to say what will become of me if I continue to break more limits?"
Kent looked at the large chunk of Attribute Points again and smiled. "After breaking all these limits, I will head to the past and do my best to complete the requirements and become a Pill Saint.

Gaia said she had fixed the Pill World Chamber, so I can now depend on the tower time while in the past. These two weeks left are more than enough to do so much, and who knows, I might just come back stronger."
Kent turned to the points and started adding them.
[Core of the Universe - Lady Universe’s POV]
From the moment Kent started retrieving his past life memories, Lady Universe knew what was about to happen. In fact, she was prepared for it ahead of time.
Naturally, Gaia should not have woken up, but she made sure she did to help Kent during the battle against the forsaken race.

However, despite doing all that, she failed to realise that Kent may have reincarnated many times, but the heart demon created when he lost Elina still followed him through the cycle of reincarnation.

Now, it had manifested itself, and Kent, who never knew of this price he had to pay for his failure, was now consumed in his rage. Even as the heart of the universe, she did not know what to do to help him.
This worried her. However, as the heart of the universe, she could not afford to get emotional, not if she wanted to avoid causing great calamity for everyone.

However, as she watched Kent put away the rest of his memory keys, she sighed, knowing his mindset had weakened somehow, and if nothing was done quickly to address the damage, things would get ugly very soon.
"I have to let the flow of time pass naturally. If I interfere to help him this once, who knows what danger may befall him in the future?"

She sighed, and after a few internal struggles, chose to take a break from watching Kent’s life. This decision was the only way she could, in a sense, handle the trauma and avoid doing anything reckless.
In the end, she stepped back and shifted her focus to someone else. This time, she chose to watch a slave girl whose life was slowly influencing the future of the universe in both good and bad ways.

chapters.title: Chapter 925: Back To The Past
paragraphs: "So, like I said, the Grand Pill Tablet will answer one question for you, so you’d better make sure to ask the right question," Kent heard Pill Monarch Nefeli’s voice, causing him to nod, though he had his brow raised.
’I guess I am back to where we left off last time.’ Kent turned around slightly and looked at the space he appeared in.
The limit breaking didn’t go as planned. It turns out his soul must reach Tier 16 before he can break the remaining limits.

Kent didn’t need that at the moment, so he chose to come back to the past and first raise his Alchemy to a higher stage, and if possible, since this is an alchemy world, he might just find a flame source he can use to form more Flame veins.
’Although there are a few minutes missing, considering I am now standing before this building while in fact, when I left the last time, we were miles away inside Pill Monarch’s Nefeli’s meeting hall’
He didn’t expect to reappear in the exact same world as before.

In a way, he had expected to appear in another of the Nine Pill Worlds left for him to explore. But now that he is in familiar territory, he quickly dismissed all other thoughts and chose to focus on the reason he had travelled 370,000 years into the past.
First, of course, was to claim the reward he had earned the last time he came.
The Grand Pill Tablet, according to Pill Monarch Nefeli, was a supreme item.
It was but a fragment of a greater treasure, said to be a Celestial Treasure. However, after it was broken into ten pieces, it regressed to the Supreme grade.
Still, this fragment, known as the Grand Pill Tablet, could answer any question one desired, provided it was related to the art of pill making.
Kent naturally has a question he wishes to ask, and so he wanted to settle that first before chasing after his main quest.
Of course, out of curiosity, and because of the friendly relationship they shared, Kent chose to ask, "If you don’t mind me asking," Kent turned to Pill Monarch Nefeli.
"Go ahead."
"Do you know someone by the name Pill Saint Flura?"

Pill Monarch Nefeli raised her brow at the mention of the familiar name. She couldn’t help but shake her head slightly at the thought that Kent, who was from a different world, would know such a name.
"Who doesn’t know that arrogant child? Although she is among the best Pill Saints in the Ten Pill Worlds, she is both rude and arrogant.
Of course, she is from a big Alchemy family in Aerithyne, the fifth-ranked Pill World, so she has the right to be arrogant.
Though I can’t help but ask, why do you ask?"
"Nothing much. It’s just that my friend Suoh mentioned she had issued some kind of challenge, and so far, nobody has managed to win."
Kent took a wild guess, believing the tower wouldn’t assign such a task as his last requirement to become a Pill Saint if challenging her would be next to impossible.

Pill Monarch Nefeli simply smiled. "Ah, that. She indeed issued a challenge several months back. Whoever below or within the Pill Saint stage who manages to defeat her in a one-on-one alchemy duel, she will hand over her participant token for the upcoming Pill Ascension Competition."
Pill Monarch Nefeli paused and looked at Kent. "You aren’t planning on accepting her challenge, are you?"
Kent laughed. "I was just asking, big sister. That said, would my status in the Pyris Pill Alliance shoot up if I were to hypothetically defeat her?"
Pill Monarch Nefeli shook her head and smiled.

"You will gain some merit and will, without a doubt, become popular. However, you must know that for someone who has been walking the pill path for decades now, she has accumulated immense experience, and in case you are unaware, the challenge she issued is to see who can concoct a better Tier 9 pill.
So far, nobody has come close to defeating her. Those who could defeat her don’t see any value in accepting her challenge since they already have a place in the upcoming Pill Ascension competition"
Kent just shook his head. "I suppose I know the question I will be asking the Grand Pill Tablet now."
Pill Monarch Nefeli looked at him for a few seconds and shook her head. "Don’t waste your only question on how to defeat her. It is not worth it.
Although joining the Pill Ascension Competition will be great for a beginner, you must be at least a Pill Sage to qualify.
So don’t waste your one question."
"I won’t be wasting it, Big Sister. And rest assured, I will defeat her in her own game and become a Pill Sage before this Pill Ascension Competition"
Pill Monarch Nefeli nodded and pointed at a stone door. A greenish smoke flew from her finger and landed on the door.
It trembled slightly, emitting a humming sound, before slowly opening.
"Go in. The moment your question is answered, you can choose to leave by willing it. However, if your question is not answered before the ten days are up, you will still be teleported out."
Kent nodded and walked into the cave.
The stone door closed behind him.
After he left, Pill Monarch Nefeli sighed deeply.
"This Kent is not only resourceful but dangerous. Just now, when he looked at me, it felt as though I was staring into the eyes of a Primal Predator."
Just thinking about it made her body tremble slightly. "I’d better be careful around him, or he might affect my Dao Heart. Who knows how hard I worked to create this persona."
Her mind drifted back to her life before she became an Alchemist, and a faint smile appeared on her face. "Master said she would be in seclusion for 500,000 years. It has already been 130,000 years.
I have suppressed my cultivation base from Level 8 Heavenly Ascension to Level 7 Spirit Lord, just so I wouldn’t draw suspicion from my master’s enemies and mine.
If I were to falter now and reveal too much, who knows what would happen to me."
She looked in the direction of the stone door and sighed. "Master, you should succeed in comprehending the intent hidden within that sword stroke left behind by Lord Genesis before coming out.
I will do my best to become an Immortal once I consume that pill."

She smiled, reading through the pill recipe Kent had given her. "Though it won’t take long now, considering this genius boy named Kent has just handed me something that could drive even Supremes to claw their faces."
After standing there for a few minutes, she left and returned to the last floor of the Pyris Pill Pagoda. She took out a communication crystal and activated it.

"Pill Emperor Hakan, I want you to go to Aerithyne and keep a close eye on that arrogant Pill Saint. A friend of mine will be coming to challenge her, and while he is strong and capable, this is a Supreme High World, and we both know there are hidden dangers everywhere. So, when the time comes, ensure he is safe."
"I will use my life to shield him if it comes to that."
Although the other end of the call exaggerated a bit, Pill Monarch Nefeli nodded and ended the call.
"Kent Madson, just who are you?" After muttering this last line, she closed her eyes to meditate.
[Kent vs. the Grand Pill Tablet]
Meanwhile, as Kent appeared on the other side of the stone door, a glowing green tablet, about 8 feet tall and 7 feet wide, greeted him.
Kent immediately felt an overwhelming attraction to it. It was almost like a younger brother reuniting with his elder sibling after a long time apart.
This strange familiarity drew Kent closer to the Grand Pill Tablet until he gently touched it. The instant he did, he felt a prick on his finger as the tablet drew his blood.
Then a voice filled the room.
"Although you are much weaker and less handsome, you smell and taste like my master. This can only mean you have reincarnated and now carry his bloodline and memories.
I miss you so much, Master."
Kent, who hadn’t expected this turn of events, raised his brow in shock. But his surprise didn’t end there.
The moment the voice echoed, a charming young girl dressed in white, appearing no older than ten, emerged from the Grand Pill Tablet, causing Kent to instinctively take a few steps back.

She looked in the direction of the stone door and sighed.
"Master, you should succeed in comprehending the intent hidden within that sword stroke left behind by Lord Genesis before coming out.
I will do my best to become an Immortal once I consume that pill."
She smiled, reading through the pill recipe Kent had given her.
"Though it won’t take long now, considering this genius boy named Kent has just handed me something that could drive even Supremes to claw their faces."
After standing there for a few minutes, she left and returned to the last floor of the Pyris Pill Pagoda.
She took out a communication crystal and activated it.
"Pill Emperor Hakan, I want you to go to Aerithyne and keep a close eye on that arrogant Pill Saint.
A friend of mine will be coming to challenge her, and while he is strong and capable, this is a Supreme High World, and we both know there are hidden dangers everywhere.
So, when the time comes, ensure he is safe."
"I will use my life to shield him if it comes to that."
Although the other end of the call exaggerated a bit, Pill Monarch Nefeli nodded and ended the call.
"Kent Madson, just who are you?" After muttering this last line, she closed her eyes to meditate.
[Kent vs. the Grand Pill Tablet]
Meanwhile, as Kent appeared on the other side of the stone door, a glowing green tablet, about 8 feet tall and 7 feet wide, greeted him.
Kent immediately felt an overwhelming attraction to it.
It was almost like a younger brother reuniting with his elder sibling after a long time apart.
This strange familiarity drew Kent closer to the Grand Pill Tablet until he gently touched it.
The instant he did, he felt a prick on his finger as the tablet drew his blood.
Then a voice filled the room.
"Although you are much weaker and less handsome, you smell and taste like my master.
This can only mean you have reincarnated and now carry his bloodline and memories.
I miss you so much, Master."
Kent, who hadn’t expected this turn of events, raised his brow in shock.
But his surprise didn’t end there.
The moment the voice echoed, a charming young girl dressed in white, appearing no older than ten, emerged from the Grand Pill Tablet, causing Kent to instinctively take a few steps back.

chapters.title: Chapter 926: The Grand Pill Tablet Spirit
paragraphs: "This is..." Kent was left dumbfounded, unsure of how to handle what he was seeing.
The young lady, or more accurately, the young girl, looked at Kent with her big eyes, which made her look charming. She turned sideways to see if Kent would recognise her.
However, after five minutes, when Kent showed no sign of recognising her, she pouted. The look on her disappointed face only made her appear much cuter and irresistible.
"Sorry, but I don’t recall ever being your master. But even if I were your master, I currently have no memory of that life since I recently reincarnated."
"I understand, Master. But I was hoping you would at least recognise me. Nana has been lonely for a very long time."
A sad expression appeared on the young girl’s face.
Kent, who saw this, felt his heart break slightly.

"Although I can’t recall the part of my life where you came in, I now have the Primordial Pill Records up to the Pill Grandmaster stage. So if you and I were related, then I am sure very soon, I will become aware of you."
Hearing this, Nana brightened up and smiled.
"The master has the Primordial Pill Records?"
Watching her smile, Kent also smiled and answered, "Yes. I have the records."
"Great. Then this time, the master will have much more success in the pill path than before." Nana circled around Kent, her giggles filling the room.
"Has the master already accomplished Batch Extraction, Double Concoction, Pill Flame Merge, or any of the basic stuff?" Nana looked at Kent with a glint in her eyes.
If one didn’t know better, they would think she was the master and Kent the disciple.
Kent smiled weakly. "I haven’t yet had the chance to go that far in the Pill Path."
Pah!
Somebody smacked the back of Kent’s head, causing him to laugh.
"Let me guess," Nana looked at him closely and said, "You are a swordsman now, so you chose to waste your time with the sword when you should be paying attention to your Alchemy path.
I can’t say I am disappointed in you simply because you are my master, but I know if this continues, you will become a vegetable."
Nana clapped her hands behind her and pondered with an ancient face, almost as if she were thinking of the best punishment to give Kent.
"We can’t have this. You are a Pill Grandmaster. Back then, you could concoct Tier 9 Pills while at the Pill Grandmaster stage. In fact, you were even able to touch 70% purity for Tier 10 pills.
How come you are talentless this time around?"

"Can’t say I am talentless. I have already attained four Pill Enlightenments, awakened my Soul Flame, and can concoct Tier 8 pills. I now have the required Pill Flame grade to concoct Tier 9 pills with some practice.
However, if you help me with what I came here for, I wouldn’t even need to practice before outright concocting Tier 9 pills. So I can’t say I’m wasted or talentless."
Nana looked at Kent for a few minutes before letting out a sigh.
"I guess it’s to be expected. If I remember correctly, you had plans to walk a different path if you were to reincarnate. So while your past was for pills, the future is for other things.
However, since you still have a thing for pill making, I will naturally help you. But first, I have a request that you can’t deny."
Kent raised his brow, hearing Nana’s childish tone. He wanted to tell her he was the master, but after hearing his failures listed to him, he just sighed.
"I am listening."
"I can tell you are at the barrier, almost at the stage of a Pill Saint. So once you reach the Pill Saint Stage, go to the world that these people call Drakthys.
There is someone named Yuna. She is an apprentice to some good-for-nothing Pill King. Kill the Pill King and free this Yuna. Afterwards, bring her here."
"I will do as you say, Master Nana." Kent laughed, "But if you don’t mind me asking, who is this Yuna?"
Nana smiled. "You might not remember yet, but back when you were at your prime, you once met somebody who had a rare body constitution called the Immortal Pill Body.
You helped her when she desperately needed it, and after helping her, she gave you a drop of her blood. That drop was what helped you become a Pill Immortal." Nana paused.
"I know I don’t have to tell you this yet, but I have been tracking that benefactor’s lineage and, at the moment, this Yuna is the only one left that I know of.
I have nine more pieces scattered in nine different worlds. From time to time, I use them to sense several million miles in search of her bloodline, but so far, only this Yuna has been found.

I know this doesn’t align with your objectives for coming here, but if she were to be discovered as someone possessing a Pill Body, her freedom would be taken from her, and she would forever become an ingredient for her captor.
So bring her here and hand her over to the lady who opened this place for you."
"I see. I will do that. However, why give her to Pill Monarch Nefeli?"
Nana just smiled. "Because she has a piece of your inheritance, meaning I have access to her soul. If she were to try anything funny, I would end her existence with a snap of my finger."
A red glow appeared in Nana’s eyes for a moment, making Kent smile weakly. The harmless Nana was more dangerous than one would expect.
"But aside from that, she is a good person. She is also talented, and you seem to have a good relationship with her. So this will be the best time to cement that relationship."
"You sound like an Immortal at the moment. But rest assured, I will refine this Pill King and extract his essence blood before letting him hurt this Yuna any further.
That said, I must become a Pill Saint first since I have other objectives for travelling this far to meet you."
"You want to know how to merge your Soul Flame with the Nine Nirvana Flames in your body," Nana smiled adorably at Kent.
Kent frowned for a moment before nodding.
"How did you know that? Did you read my mind?"
Nana smiled and shook her tiny head. "I don’t have to read your mind to know something like that. I can sense the Nine Nirvana Flames in your body.
Though they are weak since you haven’t begun walking the Twelve Paths of Nirvana, merging them with your Soul Flame would indeed make it powerful. However, the process is complex and painful."
"Pain is a best friend. That said, can you help me?"
"I can help you, Master. I can even do more than help you. I will first help merge the Nirvana Flames with your Soul Flame, then I will use the chaos from the merge to refine your Nirvana Armour.

And lastly, I will give you the Forbidden Flame Merging and Evolution Technique. Since you chose to walk the path of Pill and Slaughter, I can only do my best as your Pill Assistant to ensure you don’t kick the bucket anytime soon."
"Nana, have I ever told you how cute you look?" Kent cupped her cheeks and smiled cheerfully.

chapters.title: Chapter 927: Chaos Flame Upgrade, Nirvana Armour
paragraphs: "Master, sit in a lotus posture and let your soul flame flow throughout your body." Kent nodded and sat down. He closed his eyes and, after a few seconds of calming his nerves, he let his soul flame move through his body.
In an instant, Kent felt the warmth spread through his body like a parasite.
"Good." Nana nodded and moved closer to Kent.

"Master, your current soul flame is only Tier Nine. Though it is more than enough to help you in concocting Tier Nine and even Tier Ten pills, I believe that after this procedure, it will reach Tier Eleven or even Twelve, which will be enough to concoct up to Tier Thirteen or even Fourteen pills.
However, the master must know the danger that comes with having Tier Twelve and higher soul flames, especially in High Worlds."
Kent smiled and opened one eye to look at Nana. "Let me guess, they will try to catch me and devour my flames, right?"

Nana nodded. "In the world of alchemy, soul flames are the most valuable item an alchemist can have. Of course, these flames can be found by slaying flame-type beasts. However, acquiring a suitable flame spirit at higher Tiers, like Tier 12, is next to impossible.
While killing a normal Spirit Lord beast is manageable to some extent, meeting a Spirit Lord Flame beast is a whole different ball game.
So most alchemists prefer to devour the flames of their fellow alchemists."
"I see. In that case, I will be very careful," Kent spoke, but if one looked closely, they would see that an evil smirk appeared on the side of his mouth.
"The master should indeed be careful. I can sense that the master is strong, but this is a supreme high world where the person beside you is a deadly blade, and you will never know.
That said, the master can visit the Flame River and hunt at least a beast that has a Tier Nine soul flame. I will teach you a method and even create a foundation for you to use two flames at once.
This way, in places where the master cannot reveal his soul flame, he can use the secondary."
"You are the best, Nana. One day, when we meet and I can finally get back all ten pieces of that item, I will rebuild you a cute little loli body and have you follow me across the starry skies."
Nana blushed slightly. "I would love that, master. But for now, let’s focus on the flame upgrade and armour refining."
Kent nodded and lost his left eye. However, in his head, he couldn’t help but think of what Nana said.
"Supreme high worlds seem more mysterious than I expected." Kent’s mind moved and started analysing his next move.

"So far, I haven’t yet completed the first form of the Primal Body Tempering Art, so I can’t fully use it. However, thanks to those filthy forsaken warriors, I’ve managed to cultivate 5% of the first form, which has already boosted my strength twofold.

Of course, although I even killed five Heavenly Ascension stage warriors, they weren’t that strong or talented, suggesting they were of the standard of a Legacy High World, not even close to the standards of a Spirit Lord in a Great High World.
However, I also didn’t use my entire strength in killing them. Sjit, I even killed an Avatar with the strength of a Root Immortal. That makes me awesome"
Kent smiled, not realising that he had only faced the Avatar at 4% of his strength, and that he hadn’t used immortal qi; otherwise, Kent would have suffered greatly.

"Now, if I were to use the 7% access I have of my bloodline and the one thousand flame veins altogether, then I believe even Heavenly Ascension stage warriors in a Great High World will be crushed by me.
Not forgetting my Soul Universe.

However, the idea is to dominate even Supreme High Worlds, so with these three hundred days I have here, I will find ways to raise my strength and, if possible, battle a Heavenly Ascension stage warrior."

Kent smiled in his head. "Then again, if the feeling I felt from big sister Nefeli is remotely accurate, then I need to man up and train harder, for whether I choose to believe it or not, I am not invincible yet in a high world.
But I will be before ascending.
After all, my ladies and legion, after the battle with the forsaken, they now want to reach their limits inside the Planet Killer Dungeon before allowing me to ascend.

Confidently, I have this place and even the Sword Words to man up my game. When I ascend, I want the entire high world to know a monster has arrived... I want immortals to quake when they hear my name."
"I will be starting now, master."
Kent nodded, and Nana placed her slender finger on his forehead. A bone-shattering pain rocked Kent’s body when Nana’s finger touched his forehead.
He gritted his teeth as cold sweat broke on his forehead.
The pain spread throughout his body, causing Kent to clench his fist so tightly that blood started pouring from his palm.
"Endure it, master. The pain will pass soon."
Kent wasn’t in the mindset to nod to Nana’s words, as he was in so much pain that even when a day passed, he had no idea.
After three days had passed, the pain started to subside. Kent felt his body begin to grow stronger.
In truth, this strength boost had started from day one, but he was in so much pain that he couldn’t notice. Now that he did, he allowed a smile to appear on his face.
On the fourth day, Kent stopped feeling the pain, and instead, he began to feel a nourishing sensation throughout his body.
"The nourishing feeling the master is experiencing is the armour fusing with your soul flame." Nana’s voice entered Kent’s ears, causing him to nod.
If only he had known that things would have been much less painful if Nana had followed the process she had told him.
If she had first upgraded the soul flame before refining the armour, the pain would have been far less.
However, the unruly Nana knew that such a process would be time-consuming and wasteful, so she chose a method that refined the armour and upgraded the flame simultaneously.

But it didn’t come without its rewards. Aside from the powerful upgrades, Kent’s body had now adapted to pain so excruciating that he would hardly feel much if one day he were to undergo a similar process.
In a way, Nana had helped him, and that alone was more than Kent could be thankful for.
A few hours after the fifth day, two messages appeared, and the sound caused Kent to smile.
⟦Your soul flame has undergone an upgrade after merging with the Nine Nirvana Flames. Your soul flame now has all the properties of the Nine Nirvana Flames⟧
⟦Your Chaos Soul Flame has been upgraded to Tier Twelve⟧
However, a few seconds after this message appeared, another one followed, causing Kent to smile cheerfully.
⟦Congratulations. Your Nirvana Armour has been refined.⟧
⟦Your Nirvana Armour has fused with your Eternal Draconic Jade Body.⟧
⟦Your strength has improved by 300%. Your health has improved by 200%.⟧
Kent felt his body grow stronger.
"This is more like it." Kent lit his golden flame, which flickered with nine distinct colours. This display made him feel like he was on another level.

Nana looked at this with a weak smile. "Congratulations, master. I have created the foundation for you to have a second Pill Flame. That one can be used when you don’t want to draw attention to your soul flame.
Now, how about I give you a few techniques since you seem to be lacking in the techniques department when it comes to pill making?"
