chapters.title: Chapter 928: Kent, the Poorest in The Past
paragraphs: [Nine days later, after entering the Grand Pill Tablet Cave]
It has been nine days since Kent entered the Grand Pill Tablet Cave. At that moment, he was seated in a lotus posture, his eyes closed.
The aura of power and enlightenment radiated from him.
Nana stood just a few steps away, gazing at his face as if it were the only sight she had ever known.

"This is Master’s third enlightenment after transmitting the three techniques to him. If what he said was indeed true, Master has already attained seven enlightenments on the path of Alchemy." Nana smiled, her expression bright and innocent like that of a child.
"That makes it two more than when he was a Pill Grandmaster back then. Of course, it is Master—he was destined to break his own records one day."
The longer she looked at him, the clearer she saw the figure of the Master she had followed for hundreds of thousands of years.
Ten hours later, just before the ten-day limit was nearing, Kent opened his eyes, and an unmistakable light of understanding and clarity shone within them.
He rose to his feet and walked toward the tablet on the wall. After studying it for a few moments, he asked, "Nana, what is the final outcome after bringing all ten parts together?"
Nana smiled and puffed out her chest. A flicker of ruthlessness flashed in her eyes. "If all ten parts are brought together, I will become the Cauldron of Apotheosis."
Though it wasn’t necessary, Nana made the moment appear like a grand revelation, making Kent shake his head at her playful childishness.

"Master must understand that I am not an ordinary cauldron. Although you will discover it one day, know this: when I am made whole again, I will aid Master in creating the pill that every alchemist has dreamed of."
"What pill is that?" Kent asked.
But Nana only stuck out her tongue, clearly showing she had no intention of telling him.
Kent shook his head once more, realising that this was only the past. If he were ever to reunite with Nana in the future, he would certainly pry the truth out of her.
"I suppose I have to leave now." Kent turned from the tablet and walked toward the massive stone door.
He paused at the threshold and looked back at Nana. "I will bring the lady you asked me to save."
"I know you will, Master. But do not underestimate the Pill King. He is not weak in any aspect," Nana replied with a faint smile. "That is all I can say, Master."
Kent nodded. With a single thought, the stone door rumbled open, and he stepped outside.
The moment he emerged, he came face-to-face with Pill Monarch Nefeli.
"How did it go?" Pill Monarch Nefeli asked.
"I did not waste my question, if that is what worries you," Kent replied. "That said, I am ready to head to the Fifth Rank Pill World and accept that lady’s challenge."
Pill Monarch Nefeli exhaled softly, then gestured for Kent to follow. Soon, they returned to her chamber, where she took out a badge and handed it to him.
"Aerithyne is a Fifth Rank Pill World. Although most of its inhabitants are alchemists, hidden monsters lie in wait, eager to devour the unprepared.
This badge will grant you access to that world, but it will not protect you from harm. Be cautious when you arrive. The moment you win or lose, return here immediately."
Kent smiled, looked at Pill Monarch Nefeli, and said, "If you are worried about me, then don’t be. I have been through countless life-and-death situations, so I know how to handle myself.
That said, the protection you arranged for me won’t be necessary, for I planned to go to a certain place to train, and I am not sure they will be able to follow me there."
"Then hand the badge to someone else in case you win. The moment the access token to enter the Pill Ascension Competition leaves your hands, no one will bother coming after you."
Kent rose and walked toward the door. "I will do just that, Big Sister. Until then, do not trouble yourself to run to my aid if you hear that I have gotten myself into trouble."
With a faint smile, Kent left and made his way toward the city, where thousands of towering buildings stretched before his eyes.
This was the first time he had ventured outside since arriving in Pyris.
The Pyris Pagoda stood proudly at the very heart of the city. Yet, because of its grandeur and sacred significance, no other buildings had been constructed within a one-kilometre radius of it.

The city has five regions. East, West, North, South, and Central. Pyris paagoda stood at the centre of the city, situated in the Central Region. However, the Central region spans several thousand miles.
Just Pyris city alone is bigger than three Earths combined.
It stood tall, with nothing within its 1km vicinity.
Beyond that boundary, however, the city spread wide—filled with countless markets, inns, restaurants, and bustling streets alive with cultivators and alchemists.
At the very moment, Kent was strolling leisurely through the street, trying to get a feel of the city. Perhaps, if something caught his interest, he would purchase it.
After all, he was in the past, in Pyris City, the sacred land where the finest alchemists and the rarest alchemical treasures could be found.
Of course, he could depend on the tower in the future, but at this moment in the past, its abilities were limited. Other than storing items within its inner space, he could not retrieve them.

Fortunately, his sword was hidden within his Soul Universe, so he could summon it at will. As for a cauldron, he did have one, but it was sealed inside his space ring, which was not on his finger at present.
This meant he would first need to purchase a new space ring before he could even think of buying another cauldron.
Naturally, he would also need to acquire a stock of ingredients, for no true alchemist should wander about without carrying even the most basic of herbs.
Kent activated the Soul Map, narrowing its radius to just three kilometres, scanning every presence within that range.

"Just two kilometres into the city, and I have already spotted three Heavenly Ascension stage cultivators." A smile tugged at Kent’s lips, but then he paused in the middle of the road and scratched his head.
"Shit," he muttered.
"Hey, handsome, watch where you’re going!"
"Look at his bony arms. I’m sure he just remembered he hasn’t eaten in years—that’s why he stopped," another scoffed.
His sudden halt drew irritated shouts from passersby. One big-bellied man seemed more interested in mocking Kent’s thin frame than moving along.
Kent only smiled faintly and stepped aside from the crowded road.
"All my wealth is sealed in the tower world, and the little I saved in my space ring is now beyond my reach." Kent scratched his head, a wry expression crossing his face.

When he first came to the past, he was able to retrieve items from his tower. But now, after Gaia adjusted the time difference, something that synced the flow of time in the Pill world to match the tower, some of its functions had ceased to work.

"Thankfully, I kept the badge Big Sister gave me in my pocket. But now... I need money." Kent’s gaze swept across the busy streets, filled with merchants bargaining and customers rushing about their day.

For a fleeting moment, the idea of robbing someone crossed his mind. Yet, as a man who had once been unimaginably wealthy, he brushed the thought aside with disdain. Instead, he fell silent, pondering.
After a few moments of thought, Kent narrowed his options to three.
"It is either I sell write and sell martial techniques, concoct and sell pills, or sell one of the flying swords stored in my Soul Universe."

The possibilities made him smile again, but the expression quickly faded. "If I sell a sword, I’ll have to remove my imprint from it and place an inheritance restriction instead. The problem is, I don’t know how to do that."
And just like that, the richest in the Medium worlds has just become the poorest 370,000 years in the past.

chapters.title: Chapter 929: Finding Solutions
paragraphs: "Oh, this is bad," Kent said, walking from the side of the road and finding a place to sit. He needed to calm down first before making any more moves.
His mind was moving at an unprecedented speed.
When he asked Gaia to fix the Pill World, she told him that some things would have to be removed if she were to sync the time of the tower with that of the Pill World.

Naturally, one of those things was Kent’s ability to take anything from the tower storage. At first, he didn’t put much emphasis on that and planned to work around it before entering the Pill World again.

However, because of what happened when he tried to break his limits, and the fact that he wasn’t in the right mindset after discovering what happened to Elina during the primordial era, he entered the Pill World without any planning.
Now, not only is he broke, but he also cannot figure out how to make money.
"If I were to concoct pills and sell them, I would need ingredients and a cauldron, which I don’t have because I have no money on me.
Then again, if I were to write a few techniques and sell them, I would make more money. The only thing is, I don’t have the necessary scroll and ink to do that either.
Let’s not forget that selling one of my refined swords is nearly impossible. Lastly, I can’t leave the Pill World until the 300 days are up."
Kent scratched the back of his head and started to think again. Ten minutes later, he was still no closer to finding a sound solution.
"Maybe I should just go back and ask big sister for some money," he thought. The moment this idea entered his mind, Kent shook it off and then stood up.

"I know she will give me as much as I want, but I don’t feel like that will be appropriate. Of course, I could use the fact that I have given her heaven-defying pill recipes to take a couple of million spirit stones.
However, that would just be too shameless of me," Kent started walking again while his mind worked on coming up with a solution.
⟦The master is forgetting he has something else inside his Soul Universe⟧
Kent nearly paused when he heard the tower’s voice enter his head. However, because of what had happened earlier when he stood in the road, this time he managed to control himself and kept walking.
’Tower, how can you speak? I thought Gaia said you cannot talk to me,’ Kent asked with a slightly relieved tone.
Aside from losing access to the tower storage, he also could not speak with the tower, or at least that was what Gaia said.
⟦I am merely borrowing the days the master has to speak. Every minute spent talking to you is a day off your time limit here⟧
Kent nodded in his head. He knew Gaia was always considerate. She wouldn’t create something without adding a backdoor.
He knew how important the tower was to Kent.
However, hearing that his days were being eaten away by the tower was already a sign that he shouldn’t depend on it too much.
’It is good to hear your voice, tower. However, what else can I use to earn some money aside from the refined swords?’

⟦The master has the Soul Flag inside the Soul Universe. I calculated you might make this mistake after the issue with the Limit Breaker and your memories, so I placed the Soul Flag in the Soul Universe.
All you have to do is find a Soul Temple or auction house and auction off any of the soul spirits inside the flag.
You have five Heavenly Ascension stage soul spirits, four hundred and five Spirit Lords, and thousands of others. You can auction any and use the money to make more money.
But the master should be careful, a preserved soul spirit is a hot commodity many will kill for. Additionally, those inside the Soul Flag have been nurtured in the Soul Universe, making them unique.⟧
Kent’s eyes lit up when he heard what the tower had to say. He never knew the tower would come through for him.
Now that it had, Kent couldn’t be any happier.
’Thank you, tower.’
⟦You are welcome, master. I will be unavailable to speak with you for the next sixty days, so please be cautious. And remember, you are in a Supreme High World⟧
Kent smiled happily as he moved through the busy street. He had his soul map spread out as he searched for the nearest auction house.
He only needed to sell a Spirit King Soul Spirit, and then he would know what to do next. Naturally, Kent didn’t even know soul spirits were valuable.
He had only stored them as ingredients for refining swords. But now that he had discovered they could be used for much more, he began to wonder what else they might be useful for.
"I guess I will find out more after I get some spirit stones," Kent muttered as he spotted a grand auction house, which made him recall his first visit to an auction.

It was when he went to the Silver Leaf Auction House with Unity. Back then, he merely wanted to sell some pills and make a few spirit stones. However, he ended up meeting the woman with the most magnificent butt he had ever seen.
Thinking about it now, he realised that if he hadn’t gone to sell those Tier 0 and Tier 1 pills, he wouldn’t have met Alina.
"Auction houses are the best," Kent smiled and began moving toward the location.
"I’d better be careful then. The place I’m heading to has four Heavenly Ascension stage auras. If I didn’t know better, I would say today is a mega auction."
As he drew closer to the auction house, Kent started to wonder if his guess was correct. A few minutes later, after his soul map covered the entire building, he froze in his steps again.

Thankfully, this time there was no crowd on the road, so nobody hurled insults at him. "This is crazy. Just how common are Heavenly Ascension stage cultivators to the point that Ten can be found in one place?"
Kent looked toward the large tower standing three kilometres away from him.
"Their auras are anything but weak. If I didn’t know better, I would even assume they are beyond the stage of Heavenly Ascension."
For the first time, Kent realised that even if he used his bloodline power and Flame Veins, he wouldn’t be able to handle five of them the way he did with the Forsaken Elders.
A smile appeared on his face. "If a Pill World has this many powerful experts, then how dangerous would a Sword World or Dragon world be?"
"I must become stronger"

He started walking again. "I have already spent ten days here. Before I leave, I must form my Blood Core Gate and add at least nine thousand more Flame Veins. If possible, I must even form a Flame Core.
My ladies and the Legion would have already challenged the fourth floor, or are about to do so. I calculated that they will be able to reach the sixth floor before they can’t go any further.
By then, I should be ready to ascend to a High World. Although I have the Pill World to come and train there, a lot can change in three hundred and seventy thousand years, so I must ascend."
With that resolve, Kent started moving toward the Brown Maple Auction House. A few minutes later, he approached the tall tower.
"Stop right there, human..." A dark elf guard shouted, releasing his Spirit Sovereign cultivation toward Kent.

chapters.title: Chapter 930: Placing An Auction
paragraphs: From afar, Kent saw the two guards, so he was prepared to handle them.
One of them was a Dark Elf with greenish hair, and the other was a human with red hair, clearly marking him as a Flame Human.
Kent was already aware of the type of humans on this side of the universe. His past incarnation as Jest had interacted with Elemental Humans before, so he wasn’t too shocked to see them now, either.
Even Pill Monarch Nefeli is a Plant Human, or as most call them, Wood Humans.
Kent stopped when the Dark Elf spoke.

With his cultivation, it was only natural for him to halt when a Spirit Sovereign gave a command. Of course, Kent chose not to cause trouble, especially when there were dozens of Heavenly Ascension stage powerhouses around.
"Today is a Quarter Auction at the Brown Maple Auction House. It has already started, so go back and return tomorrow."
In a twist, the Dark Elf didn’t speak arrogantly as one might have expected. He merely said what any normal person in his place would have said.
Kent sighed, a disappointed look flashing across his face. "Too bad. I guess I will take my business elsewhere."
Kent turned and was about to leave when the Flame Human spoke. "If you don’t mind me asking, little brother, what do you want to sell?"
A smile appeared on Kent’s face as he turned back to look at the two guards.
"I was told that if I want to auction anything soul-related, I should come to the Brown Maple Auction House.

Naturally, I didn’t know today was auction day, since I had only just arrived in this city. However, I believe that if you allow me to enter and display my commodity, the auction house will see a bountiful sale today."

If at first Kent wanted to auction a Spirit King, then upon sensing ten Heavenly Ascension stage monsters inside the auction house, he raised his aim to a Spirit Lord. And it wasn’t just any ordinary Spirit Lord—Kent was aiming to sell a Spirit Soul from the Forsaken Race.

He had already done his research before coming to the Pill World. From what he knew, because of the World’s limitation immunity on Forsaken warriors, their bodies and souls were a hot commodity in the universe.
So Kent wanted to make sure his pocket was filled once again. Being rich in the future had made him a heavy spender, so he intended to walk away with a bountiful harvest today.
The two guards looked at each other, then smiled at Kent. "We may be able to allow you to enter. But how sure are you that what you have will even be accepted before putting it on sale?"
Kent smiled faintly and leaned in toward the two guards. "How does a Tier 16 Soul Spirit sound?"
The two guards widened their eyes at what Kent had just said.
Kent had merely lowered the rank of the soul spirit to a mere Spirit Monarch since he knew that claiming it was a Spirit Lord would frighten them. Even a Spirit Sovereign would leave them gobsmacked.
"Are you sure?" the Dark Elf asked, and Kent nodded.
"I can show you if you want to see." Kent smiled, almost appearing like a clueless child who didn’t know the dangers of this world.
The two guards looked at each other, and for a moment, Kent expected them to nod to his request. However, they shook their heads, and one of them took out a communication crystal and activated it.
"Lady Wu, there is a... uhm... There is a skinny human here who claims to have a Tier 16 Soul Spirit that he wants to auction. Should we allow him in, or should we send him packing?"
’I am not skinny.’ Kent instinctively looked at his hand for a split second before sighing.
’Maybe I should eat more.’
"Okay, Lady Wu, " the guard put away the communication crystal and stared at Kent. He didn’t immediately speak. He studied Kent’s posture for a few seconds before stepping out of the way.
"You can enter. Lady Wu will personally meet you inside"

Kent smiles and nods. "Thank you, seniors," he said with a nod. With that, he moved past them and entered the auction house. The moment he entered, Kent felt all forms of restraints working in sync to keep the tower in place and secure as ever.

Just the ground floor was already too large, and thousands of people will be able to walk freely inside. ’From the outside, it doesn’t look this big, but now inside, it feels like a small town in here, ’ Kent said to himself as he looked around.
There aren’t many people around, probably because today is an auction day.
Suddenly, Kent felt a pair of eyes land on him, causing him to instinctively turn. From a distance, he saw a lady dressed in purple cloths walking toward him.
Kent activated the enchanted eyes and looked at the woman. He saw she was a Spirit Monarch, just one step away from reaching the Spirit Sovereign stage.
The air of nobility emanated from her, indicating she was no ordinary person. Kent waited for her to get close.
"You are the one with the Soul Spirit, " the woman asked, and this time Kent sensed the arrogance he expected from the guards.
"That will be me. My name is Kent" Kent introduced himself, but Lady Wu doesn’t seem interested in that. Instead, she was more focused on the Soul Spirit.
Kent didn’t seem offended. He expected to be treated like that, considering he was but a mere core formation expert. He waved his hand, and a soul flag appeared.
Lady Wu raised her brow slightly when the soul flag appeared. However, she showed no obvious reaction, which showed she couldn’t wait to see what Kent had to offer.
"Naturally, I wanted to auction a Tier 16 Soul Spirit, but after the warm reception I received from the two senior guards outside, I decided to auction a Tier 18 Soul Spirit from the..."
Kent paused and slightly looked at Lady Wu before shaking the soul flag,
From within, a soul spirit flew out, bringing a chilling feeling to the surroundings. "From the Forsaken Race"
Lady Wu, who held a calm and distant expression, suddenly took a few steps back, with a shocked expression painting her face.

Kent shook the flag, and a second Tier 18 Forsaken Soul Spirit appeared, multiplying the shock on Lady Wu’s face. The next second, however, Kent waved the flag, and the Soul Spirits vanished back inside, and the soul flag vanished from sight.
He smiled at Lady Wu before asking, "So what do you think. Do my commodities qualify to be auctioned off in your humble auction house?"
Lady Wu held her shocked expression for a couple of minutes, unsure of what to say. However, while she wasn’t speaking, her head was nodding the whole time.
After recovering, she looked at Kent with a respectful gaze, one that Kent knew wouldn’t change for generations to come.
"Little brother, if you don’t mind me asking, do you intend to auction both Soul Spirits?"
Kent smiled and shook his head, "I will sell only one", he paused and read Lady Wu’s expression, which had turned dull, "But I might put the second one up for auction after observing your services"
Her expression brightened up hearing Kent’s last words. "Little brother, why don’t we put one up for auction now.
Today is our Quarterly Auction event. Although it had already begun, there is one more round of sales to come. We can add yours as the last item."
"Lead the way, Lady Wu..."

chapters.title: Chapter 931: Offer
paragraphs: After seeing the value of what Kent was selling, Lady Wu transformed from a nonchalant, arrogant lady into one who wanted to cosy up to Kent and ensure she got what she wanted.
Naturally, Kent didn’t have any issue making her feel happy. He knew how having connections could help him in the long run.
Especially if he managed to form a good relationship with someone from the past, he might reap the benefits in the future. One of the many perks of having the means to visit the past.
Kent already had that in mind, so he wasn’t about to take everything personally and frown when he should smile.
A short while later, they entered Lady Wu’s office. She immediately served Kent a cup of tea with a smile on her face.
Kent took a sip and smiled. "Good tea."
"Thank you, little brother."
"You can just call me Kent."
Lady Wu nodded and unfurled a scroll. "Kent, if you don’t mind me asking, are you already affiliated with any auction house in this city?"
"No."
"Wonderful." Lady Wu took out a platinum badge from a drawer in her desk and presented it to Kent.

"This is the highest grade of badge our Brown Maple Auction House has. All individuals with this badge are considered VIP customers. Now you are one of them, and if you want, I can make you a VIP seller in this auction house.
Becoming a VIP seller means your goods will receive top priority among the thousands of goods we auction every week.

Also, as a VIP seller, you will have a 20% discount on all things you buy, and depending on your selling value, we might even cut you in for a share of our auction house in this world and all other worlds out there."
Kent took a sip of the wine again and set the cup down. "That sounds like a good thing."
"It’s indeed a good thing. With even 1% share of our auction house, you will earn millions every single week. Trust me, this is a good thing."
"In that case, I am ready to join your humble auction house. However, why don’t we talk about the commodity I want to sell today?"
Lady Wu was overjoyed. If this deal went through, her stock would skyrocket like a moving bus. In a way, she would be earning even more than Kent.

Aside from that, with her new status after this sale went through, she would not only manage more than one auction house belonging to Brown Maple Auction House, but also oversee the management of more than 30 other auction houses.
But that would only be if she sold a Tier 18 Soul Spirit from a Forsaken Race. If she were to sell a second one, her role in Brown Maple Auction House would skyrocket even further.
"There are still three things left to auction. However, since I promised to make your item the last, I still stand by that promise.
However, I must ask, do you really plan to sell this today? Our annual auction is just three months away. If this were to be sold there, you would become a rich man."
Kent shook his head. "I need it sold today. You can sell the second one during that period."
"Very well. In that case, the auction house will take 10% of the amount the item is sold for. The rest will be given to you.
However, since you have chosen to join our humble establishment, I will open an account in your name, and any proceeds you earn will be deposited there, which you can easily withdraw with a thought.
I will prepare everything by the time the auction closes today."
"That will be great then. Also, if you don’t mind me asking, what will be the opening price for the soul spirit?"
"The opening bid will be priced at 200 million High-Grade Spirit Stones."
Kent smiled weakly, knowing he would soon be walking away with some cash on him. "Then I will wait for good news." He leaned back in his chair and started sipping his tea.
"You can observe the auction if you want. Now that you are a VIP customer, you can come and go as you please."
Kent nodded. He gave the soul spirit to Lady Wu, who used a device Kent had never seen before to collect it. She then led Kent to a private room before leaving to attend to her business.
When Kent arrived in the room, a Tier 14 pill was being auctioned. The bidding war was heated.
"120 million," a voice came from the middle rooms. However, it was quickly overshadowed by another voice coming from yet another middle room.

Kent noticed the auction hall had been divided into three segments. The ground level was an open space, occupied by those who weren’t of much class or important enough to make a difference in the auction house.
The middle level comprised middle-class families and influential individuals, such as those in the lower ranks of the Pill Alliance or sects.
As for the top floor, where Kent was, that place was reserved for the VIPs.
At the moment, a bidding war was raging between the various rooms on the middle floor, showing that the Tier 14 pill was something they would benefit from. The top floor, however, remained silent.

Kent used the soul map to see if he could see through the formation inside the rooms. He failed to see their faces, but he didn’t come out empty-handed. He managed to determine their cultivation bases.

All ten Heavenly Ascension stage experts he sensed were in the top-floor rooms, indicating they were dignitaries. But then again, who would be dumb enough not to make Heavenly Ascensions stage cultivators VIPs?
"Looks like I must increase my soul strength some more if I want to be able to see through formations in High Worlds," Kent said to himself.

A few minutes later, the pill was auctioned for 240 million spirit stones. Naturally, if these 240 million spirit stones were sent to a Medium World, they would be equivalent to 24 billion spirit stones.

The reason was that in the High Worlds, they used High-Grade Spirit Stones instead of the low-grade ones used in Medium Worlds. One High-Grade Spirit Stone was equivalent to 100 low-grade spirit stones.
This showed that life in the High World was much more expensive than in the Medium World.
The next item was brought in, but Kent showed no interest in it, despite it being a core ingredient in the concoction of most pills.
He wouldn’t want to make an offer he couldn’t pay for. To him, if he had enough money, he could always buy the Omega Spirit Fruit any day.
After the Omega Spirit Fruit was sold, another item went for a staggering 300 million spirit stones. Then the next item, meant to be the last, was brought out.

It was an old armour that could no longer be worn and was discarded because it was beyond repair. However, the reason it was placed at a starting bid of 90 million spirit stones was because of the immortal aura emanating from it.
According to the auctioneer, the armour contained a trace of Immortal Aura.

Naturally, mortals had no business playing around with items meant for immortals. However, if one were to cultivate this aura, not only would their body be tempered with immortal energy, but it would also enrich their Spirit Energy and make breaking through to the Empyrean stage much safer.
"So that was what they came here for." The moment the armour was brought out, the ten Heavenly Ascension stage experts leaned forward.
Kent felt the air grow thick with tension.
"This will be a good show... though in the end, I will be stealing it from the one who ends up buying it." An evil smile appeared on Kent’s face as he began to watch the bidding war.

chapters.title: Chapter 932: Unofficial Owner of the Immortal Armour
paragraphs: "140 Million"
A voice came from one of the VIP rooms marked Ten.
However, the next second, another voice overshadowed him.
"180 million"
"190 million"
"195 million"
The bidding war had just begun, yet the price tag had already surpassed 200 million and was still climbing rapidly.
All this was happening between the ten Heavenly Ascension stage cultivators seated on the top floor of the auction hall.
Kent remained in his seat, watching with a smile that only he understood.
’They are rich, that much is true, but so what? At the end of the day, I will be the owner of this armour. You ten are merely vying to become temporary owners.’ A smirk tugged on his lips.
"230 Million"
The bid went up again. However, none of the ten Heavenly Ascension cultivators seemed close to the limit of what they were willing to spend that day. They kept bidding.
In no time, the bid reached 300 million. Within the next 30 minutes, it had entered half a billion. By that time, a new voice joined the bidding war.
This time, Kent focused his attention on the newcomer, but he failed to estimate their cultivation base. Still, he sensed danger from the voice that spoke.
It was a lady’s voice.
The moment she placed her bid, a one-minute pause ensued.

Nobody raised the bid after she spoke. This made Kent wonder just what kind of existence she was. Soon, he began to suspect that the lady who had placed the bid was someone even the Heavenly Ascension stage cultivators dared not offend.
"700 Million"
To everyone’s shock, a VIP room that had been quiet since the start suddenly came alive, and murmurs spread through the hall.
Kent used the Soul Map to listen in on some of these murmurs.
"I recognise that voice... She is the Sect Leader of the Heaven’s Eye Sect."

"Oh... Now that you mention it, I was wondering where I had heard that voice before. No wonder the others dare not bid higher... After all, going against a Peak Heavenly Ascension stage expert is not something they want."
"But who is the one who just raised the bid? I don’t recognise his voice."
"I think I do. The man must be the Vice Sect Leader of the Blue Flame Pill Palace."
"Are you sure? The last time I heard, the Vice Leader of the Blue Flame Pill Palace fell into the Flame River while pursuing one of the Flame River Monarchs. How is he here then?"
"I don’t know how, but I recognise that voice... It is him."
"If he is here, then it seems he will be walking away with this armour."

"Such a pity. From what I’ve heard, the Blue Flame Pill Palace has been aiming for the title of the greatest pill society in Pyris. If he manages to get this armour, that dream might just become reality."
"It seems so. But who could blame him? In the end, it is the strong who get the best end of the deal, while we, the weak and poor, can only watch."
"Too sad. Even if the Sect Leader of Heaven’s Eye buys it, leaving the city dominated by the Blue Flame Pill Palace will be extremely hard."
Kent continued listening to the murmurs. Every word revealed something, but the loudest message was the danger both bidders represented.
The two were powerful, and the fact that even his Soul Map could not estimate their strength was already enough. Still, his plan to steal the armour from whoever won it had not changed.
’I’d better plan it well. This armour is mine for the future, and there is nothing any of you can do.’
Still, Kent knew he had to be careful.
’The Flame River, huh... I suppose I’ll head there next after I defeat that arrogant Pill Saint and become a Pill Saint myself.

I have many things to accomplish, with the most important being the formation of my flame veins and, if possible, a flame core. That way, even if I were to clash with these people, escaping would not be an issue.’
Kent paused for a moment. At that time, the bid had risen to 900 million...
’If I manage to form at least a Life Blood Seal, then winning against a Peak Heavenly Ascension stage expert who is an alchemist should be manageable.
I can’t say I can compete with Sword Emperors yet, but I have the means to handle Alchemists who aren’t well-versed in combat.’
The bid entered 1 billion and continued to rise slowly.
’Then again, if I form a flame core and twenty-five thousand flame veins, and even go ahead to form my first Blood Core Gate...
Then all three, in addition to 9% of my bloodline power and a potential Blood Life Seal, I believe it will be enough to take them on alone.
I need to work hard here, and hopefully, I will return to the future as a different person.’
"1.3 Billion." The man placed a new bid, and this time, the lady didn’t counter. After a few minutes of silence, the auctioneer declared the man the winner.
Kent sensed a sneer and a prideful air emanating from the VIP room where the man who won the bid was seated. This caused Kent to sneer as well.
’Hold on to my treasure for me, mister. I will be taking it off your hands soon enough.’
The auctioneer looked around and smiled.
"Everyone... Although this armour was promised to be the last item for sale today, we have just received a last-minute item that we cannot afford to hide away.
So there will be one final item up for auction."
The Murmurs that were spreading everywhere after the man from the Blue Flame Pill Palace won the bid slowly died down. Everyone wanted to hear about the new item.
In an auction, it was well known that the last item sold was often a heaven-defying treasure, so naturally, they wanted to hear about this treasure and, if possible, join a bidding war to claim it.
Inside the VIP rooms, those who were ready to leave suddenly changed their minds. They hadn’t expected one last item, so they chose to stay.
Even the lady who had lost the bid to the Vice Leader of the Blue Flame Pill Palace remained.
"The next item is something most of you know all too well, yet this one will shock you. It is a Soul Spirit. However, this Soul Spirit isn’t an ordinary one."
The auctioneer paused, and for a moment, one could see shock and greed flash across his face. That expression only made everyone shift slightly in their seats.
If an item up for sale could evoke such emotions in the auctioneer, then it had to be something extraordinary.
"The last item for sale is a Tier 18 Soul Spirit from the Forsaken Race. Bidding starts at 200 million."
For a moment, Kent felt the entire auction house grow cold. He sensed the shock in the air, and silence fell...
But then, the bidding war erupted, and the entire auction house came alive.

The bidding war had just begun, yet the price tag had already surpassed 200 million and was still climbing rapidly.
All this was happening between the ten Heavenly Ascension stage cultivators seated on the top floor of the auction hall.
Kent remained in his seat, watching with a smile that only he understood.
’They are rich, that much is true, but so what?
At the end of the day, I will be the owner of this armour.
You ten are merely vying to become temporary owners.’ A smirk tugged on his lips.
"230 Million"
The bid went up again.
However, none of the ten Heavenly Ascension cultivators seemed close to the limit of what they were willing to spend that day.
They kept bidding.
In no time, the bid reached 300 million.
Within the next 30 minutes, it had entered half a billion.
By that time, a new voice joined the bidding war.
This time, Kent focused his attention on the newcomer, but he failed to estimate their cultivation base.
Still, he sensed danger from the voice that spoke.
It was a lady’s voice.
The moment she placed her bid, a one-minute pause ensued.
Nobody raised the bid after she spoke.
This made Kent wonder just what kind of existence she was.
Soon, he began to suspect that the lady who had placed the bid was someone even the Heavenly Ascension stage cultivators dared not offend.
"700 Million"
To everyone’s shock, a VIP room that had been quiet since the start suddenly came alive, and murmurs spread through the hall.
Kent used the Soul Map to listen in on some of these murmurs.
"I recognise that voice...
She is the Sect Leader of the Heaven’s Eye Sect."
Now that you mention it, I was wondering where I had heard that voice before.
No wonder the others dare not bid higher...
After all, going against a Peak Heavenly Ascension stage expert is not something they want."
"But who is the one who just raised the bid?
I don’t recognise his voice."
"I think I do.
The man must be the Vice Sect Leader of the Blue Flame Pill Palace."
"Are you sure?
The last time I heard, the Vice Leader of the Blue Flame Pill Palace fell into the Flame River while pursuing one of the Flame River Monarchs.
How is he here then?"
"I don’t know how, but I recognise that voice...
It is him."
"If he is here, then it seems he will be walking away with this armour."
"Such a pity.
From what I’ve heard, the Blue Flame Pill Palace has been aiming for the title of the greatest pill society in Pyris.
If he manages to get this armour, that dream might just become reality."
"It seems so.
But who could blame him?
In the end, it is the strong who get the best end of the deal, while we, the weak and poor, can only watch."
"Too sad.
Even if the Sect Leader of Heaven’s Eye buys it, leaving the city dominated by the Blue Flame Pill Palace will be extremely hard."
Kent continued listening to the murmurs.
Every word revealed something, but the loudest message was the danger both bidders represented.
The two were powerful, and the fact that even his Soul Map could not estimate their strength was already enough.
Still, his plan to steal the armour from whoever won it had not changed.
’I’d better plan it well.
This armour is mine for the future, and there is nothing any of you can do.’
Still, Kent knew he had to be careful.
’The Flame River, huh...
I suppose I’ll head there next after I defeat that arrogant Pill Saint and become a Pill Saint myself.
I have many things to accomplish, with the most important being the formation of my flame veins and, if possible, a flame core.
That way, even if I were to clash with these people, escaping would not be an issue.’
Kent paused for a moment.
At that time, the bid had risen to 900 million...
’If I manage to form at least a Life Blood Seal, then winning against a Peak Heavenly Ascension stage expert who is an alchemist should be manageable.
I can’t say I can compete with Sword Emperors yet, but I have the means to handle Alchemists who aren’t well-versed in combat.’
The bid entered 1 billion and continued to rise slowly.
’Then again, if I form a flame core and twenty-five thousand flame veins, and even go ahead to form my first Blood Core Gate...
Then all three, in addition to 9% of my bloodline power and a potential Blood Life Seal, I believe it will be enough to take them on alone.
I need to work hard here, and hopefully, I will return to the future as a different person.’
"1.3 Billion." The man placed a new bid, and this time, the lady didn’t counter.
After a few minutes of silence, the auctioneer declared the man the winner.
Kent sensed a sneer and a prideful air emanating from the VIP room where the man who won the bid was seated.
This caused Kent to sneer as well.
’Hold on to my treasure for me, mister.
I will be taking it off your hands soon enough.’
The auctioneer looked around and smiled.
"Everyone...
Although this armour was promised to be the last item for sale today, we have just received a last-minute item that we cannot afford to hide away.
So there will be one final item up for auction."
The Murmurs that were spreading everywhere after the man from the Blue Flame Pill Palace won the bid slowly died down.
Everyone wanted to hear about the new item.
In an auction, it was well known that the last item sold was often a heaven-defying treasure, so naturally, they wanted to hear about this treasure and, if possible, join a bidding war to claim it.
Inside the VIP rooms, those who were ready to leave suddenly changed their minds.
They hadn’t expected one last item, so they chose to stay.
Even the lady who had lost the bid to the Vice Leader of the Blue Flame Pill Palace remained.
"The next item is something most of you know all too well, yet this one will shock you.
It is a Soul Spirit.
However, this Soul Spirit isn’t an ordinary one."
The auctioneer paused, and for a moment, one could see shock and greed flash across his face.
That expression only made everyone shift slightly in their seats.
If an item up for sale could evoke such emotions in the auctioneer, then it had to be something extraordinary.
"The last item for sale is a Tier 18 Soul Spirit from the Forsaken Race.
Bidding starts at 200 million."
For a moment, Kent felt the entire auction house grow cold.
He sensed the shock in the air, and silence fell...
But then, the bidding war erupted, and the entire auction house came alive.

chapters.title: Chapter 933: Let The Bidding War Begin
paragraphs: "400 million"
"500 million"
In no time, the price crossed 500 million, and it continued to climb. The war had only just begun, but it was heated.
Be it the people in the VIP rooms or the middle rooms, everyone was bidding. Some were using their communication crystals to call home and inform their families about what was up for sale.
Naturally, these people were banking their entire fortune on the Tier 18 Forsaken Race Soul Spirit.
Kent sat calmly with a smug expression on his face as he watched all this unfold.
He didn’t understand why these people were going all out for his Soul Spirit. To him, this Soul Spirit was merely an ingredient for refining weapons.
Although Kent was fascinated by the idea of refining treasures using soul spirits, he had no idea that Soul Spirits are actually the best materials one could refine.
Instead of merely using them as ingredients to refine a sword, one could refine a Soul Spirit into a Soul Puppet.

The process is complex and time-consuming, but if one were able to refine a Soul Spirit into a Soul Puppet, then not only would they have a powerful helper, but they would also have a terrifying puppet that can’t be killed by physical attacks.
In fact, Soul Puppets are so terrifying that if they were to appear on the battlefield, many would flee with their tails between their legs.
Only soul attacks could kill them.
However, since they are Soul Puppets, one would need extremely powerful soul attacks before they can confidently say they would be able to kill a Soul Puppet.
Naturally, that is one dangerous puppet everyone with functioning brain cells would want to have.
However, while a Tier 18 Soul Spirit could cause this much chaos, the real reason this bidding war had grown to such an extent was the nature of this particular Soul Spirit.
As a Soul Spirit from the Forsaken Race, the rules did not apply to it.

This means that if it were to be refined into a Soul Puppet, not only would it ignore all cultivation restriction rules, but it would also possess the potential to be upgraded to a Tier 20 Soul Puppet, making it several times stronger than a Heavenly Ascension stage cultivator.
So with this much potential displayed before them, it is perfectly understandable to see how wild these people had become.
"1 billion!" The lady from Heaven’s Eye raised the bid into the billions, causing many to drop out of the race instantly.
They may want the soul puppet, but they aren’t that rich to bank such a fortune on it. The chance of refining failure is also a factor here.
However, while many left the bidding war, many still chose to remain.
"1.2 billion"
"1.4 billion"
"2 billion" The lady raised the price again, and this time, even the man who bought the armour went quiet.
However, Kent, who was observing everything with his Soul Map, narrowed his gaze at the man’s VIP room.
’This lady is dead,’ Kent muttered.
He sensed it, and thanks to the Soul Map, he was able to discern that the killing intent surrounding the man’s room was genuine.
The man wouldn’t be losing this soul spirit today.
If he couldn’t win it fair and square in a bidding war, then he would steal it, even if it meant killing the lady.
Kent pondered.
After a few seconds, an evil smile appeared on his face. He closed his eyes and accessed his Soul Universe.

’After forming my core, I felt like I could increase my soul strength by two more levels. I am currently at Tier 14, which is comparable to a Spirit King. If I want to break through this formation, I must reach the Tier 15 stage.’
Kent looked at the asteroid inside his Soul Universe, and a smile formed on his face.
It had become so large that Kent didn’t even know if he had gone too far.
The diameter of the asteroid, although uneven, had already stretched past 300 km. It was so massive that Kent knew if he were to unleash it, even an Immortal would find it difficult to handle.
He looked around and saw smaller versions of the asteroids and a few Soul Bombs he had prepared for emergencies.
Then there were the refined swords.
Kent estimated that if he were to reach Tier 15, the swords would become even more potent. So, he paused all operations and began channelling the Soul Essence into his own soul.
In no time, he sensed his soul growing.
’To break the next limit, my soul needs to be at Tier 16.’
Kent hadn’t initially wanted to do this. He didn’t want to waste Soul Essence on advancing his soul strength since it wasn’t urgently needed.
But at this moment, he knew it was the only way to get what he wanted—and perhaps gain an ally from the past, someone he was certain would become a big shot in the future.
After a few minutes, he neared the Tier 15 stage and broke through. The moment he did, he sensed his Soul Universe grow much stronger.
However, Kent didn’t have time to dwell on that. The bidding war had already reached 3 billion, with the lady in the lead.
The Vice Leader of the Blue Flame Pill Palace was also unwilling to back out. He wanted the Soul Spirit, which at that moment seemed even more valuable than the armour he had bought.
He even blamed himself for buying the armour.
Buying the armour rendered him low on spirit stones, only adding to his fury.
Kent opened the Soul Map again, and this time, though their formation was still intact, he was able to see through it. He first focused on the man.

’A Dark Elf, huh? No wonder he was quick to exude killing intent.’ Kent saw through the man’s cultivation, and using his Enchanted Eyes, he observed that the Dark Elf had already broken fourteen limits on his body and had also reached Tier 17 in Soul Cultivation, as well as achieved a Diamond Body in Body Cultivation.
Although his main focus was on alchemy and flame arts, making that much progress in Soul and Body Cultivation was already commendable.
Kent then looked at the lady, and for a moment, his brow rose.
’A Lightning Human.’ Kent examined the beauty with blue hair, and for a brief moment, he was impressed by what he saw.
Although she possessed the same cultivations as the Dark Elf, she lagged in the number of limits broken. She had broken twelve, meaning she was behind in her Soul and Mind.
Though the difference was only two, in combat, just two could prove catastrophic.
Aside from that, Kent could sense that the Dark Elf was not simple. There was something about him that made Kent sense some form of danger from him.
Because of this, Kent decided to use someone else’s misfortune to gain his own fortune.
He focused on the Lightning Human’s VIP room and, using the Soul Map, sent a message to her.
"You don’t know me, and I most certainly don’t know you. However, I know all about you, down to the village where you were born.
But that is not why I am here. The reason you are hearing my voice in your head like your guardian angel is because today you’re fated to die—and I am the only one who can save you."

chapters.title: Chapter 934: Value of a Forsaken Soul
paragraphs: "Who are you?"
Kent expected the lady to panic when his voice entered her head. But to his shock, she maintained her composure and even raised the bid to 4 billion before asking the question.
She knew that if someone was strong enough to break through the formation in the room, then they were worthy of her attention.
"Knowing my name isn’t the main point here. What you should be focused on is how you can walk out of this alive."
There was another pause, then the lady asked again, "Who are you?"

Kent merely smiled. "I am a nobody who wants the armour that the man bought. At first, I was planning on getting stronger before coming for it, but seeing that he plans on killing you if you win the bid for the Soul Spirit, I figured we could work together and kill two birds with one stone.

I will help you kill him, which will mean the Soul Spirit will be yours without any danger coming from anywhere, and I will get the armour. All things considered, this is the best deal you can ever have."
She raised the bid to 4.7 billion and then pondered. She had no idea Kent was watching her, so she reflected for a couple of seconds before an evil smile appeared on her face.
"Deal."
Kent smirked, knowing the lady had already made her choice.
"Let me guess, you plan to use me, then after we take him out, you will backstab me and take the armour for yourself." Kent transmitted his laughter, causing the lady to frown.
"Also, you shouldn’t smile evilly anymore. It doesn’t look good on your beautiful face."
With these words, the lady was finally made aware of the kind of person she was dealing with.
Even at her Peak Heavenly Ascension stage of cultivation and with her overpowered martial techniques, she couldn’t see through the formation.
However, somehow Kent managed to see through it and even created a communication channel between them.
This made the lady take a step back and begin to wonder just what was happening. Then she sensed it. Kent had expanded her senses to cover the VIP room of the Dark Elf.
When she saw the murderous look in the man’s eyes, she knew she was indeed in danger.

"Don’t worry about him. Just win the bid, and we will talk. And like I said, I only want the armour. So use the time to make up your mind about what you want. Either way, I am getting the armour, and if you come against me, I won’t hesitate to throw an asteroid at you... and I mean that literally."
The lady shuddered, but she didn’t make it seem obvious.
Kent, of course, saw it but chose not to dwell on it.
The auction was heated to the point that Kent started to see the killing intent of the Dark Elf clashing with the unyielding aura of the Lightning Human lady.
This was his way of warning the lady about the fate that awaited her if she didn’t back out. However, the lady, who knew the value of this Soul Spirit, was as unyielding as ever.
In no time, the price rose to 7 billion.
However, just when the price reached the 7 billion mark, it was raised to 10 billion by the lady.
Kent saw the reason. The lady was waiting for feedback from someone. Just like everyone else, she had also called home, so when she received the feedback, she went big, and it paid off.
After five whole minutes, nobody was able to bid higher than that.
"The Tier 18 Forsaken Soul Spirit is sold to the distinguished guest in VIP room 16." The auctioneer announced the winner, and the entire auction house erupted into murmurs.
By now, word had spread far and wide about the appearance of a Tier 18 Forsaken Soul Spirit. Monsters hidden in caves even heard of this, so they all started coming around.
"The auction is now over. But before we all leave, know that there is a chance another Tier 18 Forsaken Soul Spirit will be sold in the Annual Auction just three months from now.
On that note, see you all in three months’ time."
Everyone started leaving to prepare for the Annual Auction.

Kent linked up with the lady who had won the bid. "Pay for your item, disguise yourself as an ordinary person, and go find a low-key inn to stay in for the night." Kent’s words sounded more like a command in her ears, causing her to frown.
However, before she could say anything, Kent activated the full coverage of the Soul Map, showing her twenty dangers hidden and waiting for her to leave the auction house.
This caused her body to shudder.

"I am not a magician, but I know the one you are counting on to come to your aid will face some obstacles on the way. So while this is going to be difficult, just follow my advice and hide out for the night.
I will handle my business on this side, and then I will come to you tomorrow. Don’t worry, I will find you even if you hide under a rock.
And before you think I am coming for your precious Soul Spirit, know that I was the one who put it up for auction."
Kent cut the communication channel, but he continued to observe her. First, she rushed to where she could collect her item. She paid for it and quickly left.
Along the way, she entered a certain room, and after a minute, she came out looking as ordinary as she could.
"At least she is smart, disguising herself as a worker," Kent smirked, knowing this disguise was good, but he planned to make it better.

He linked up with the two guards outside. "I will give each of you 100 million high-grade spirit stones. All you have to do is act familiar with the lady who will be coming out of the auction house in 3... 2... 1..."
Right when Kent’s countdown hit zero, the lady walked out, and Kent sent out a command, "Do it."
The Dark Elf was the first to act. "Big sister Luxa, be sure to bring pancakes tomorrow too!"
The Flame Human guard also made his move. With a familiar smile, he spoke, "Yes, big sister Luxa, those pancakes were nice. I really enjoyed them."
At that moment, Kent’s voice entered the lady’s ear. "Smile and respond to them."
Though she had no idea what was happening, she forced out a smile and replied to the two guards, "Don’t worry. I will bring double what I usually bring."
"Thank you, big sister Luxa!"
"Nice one, you two. Wait for me outside. I will be out in under an hour." They recognised Kent’s voice. It was one of the reasons why they followed his command.
The lady managed to leave the auction house and quickly made her way to a low-quality inn that offered hotel services. She paid for a room and quickly entered.
As soon as she sat down, she began creating restrictions.
Meanwhile, back in the auction house, Lady Wu entered the VIP room where Kent was, a golden smile on her face.

"Thank you, big sister Luxa!"
"Nice one, you two.
Wait for me outside.
I will be out in under an hour." They recognised Kent’s voice.
It was one of the reasons why they followed his command.
The lady managed to leave the auction house and quickly made her way to a low-quality inn that offered hotel services.
She paid for a room and quickly entered.
As soon as she sat down, she began creating restrictions.
Meanwhile, back in the auction house, Lady Wu entered the VIP room where Kent was, a golden smile on her face.

chapters.title: Chapter 935: Soul Puppets
paragraphs: Lady Wu approached Kent with a beaming smile.
At first glance, Kent knew she had earned more than he. One can’t be that happy without an overwhelming reason.
Money-wise, Kent would walk away with 9 billion. However, as someone in charge of the auction house that sold the Forsaken Soul Spirit, she was destined to earn more in the coming days.
"Distinguished guest, I have compiled everything and put it in this space ring.
It contains your bank card. All you need to do now is infuse it with your soul energy, and it will forever be yours.
It will imprint your soul signature on it so that, aside from you, nobody will be able to access the vault space inside to withdraw your funds.
I have also registered you as a seller. That means from today onwards, you can place an item to be auctioned at any Brown Maple Auction House.
With these new statutes, all items placed for auction will only incur a 5% commission from us. Additionally, as a VIP seller, you are eligible for a 20% discount on all items purchased from us.
You can also utilise our information-gathering services and appraisal services at no cost.
The most important thing is that you now own 2% of this establishment’s shares. All future earnings will be deposited in your account, which you can access from anywhere.
Also, as you continue to sell items with us, your shares can increase."
Kent slid the ring onto his finger and took out his bank card. He looked inside, and just like how a space ring behaves, there was a space packed with Spirit Stones.

However, unlike space rings, Kent saw a complex formation that, with a single glance, he knew wasn’t something he could wrap his mind around. When he returns to the future, he will use the tower or Gaia to determine the nature of this formation.
He placed the card back inside his space ring and looked at Lady Wu.
"You’ve done a good job. However, I have some questions I want answers to if you don’t mind." Lady Wu nodded promptly.
"I will be happy to answer any question you have."
Kent didn’t want to comment on her enthusiasm, so he merely asked the question on his mind. "I can’t help but wonder, why did they fight over the Soul Spirit like that?
It was a mere Tier 18 Soul Spirit. I am sure they can easily kill a beast or their fellow humans and seize their Soul Spirits.
Why go all out for a mere Tier 18 Soul Spirit like that?"
Lady Wu seemed taken aback by Kent’s question. She didn’t expect someone who had sold a Tier 18 Soul Spirit to be this clueless.

Naturally, Kent knew Soul Spirits were valuable commodities. However, he didn’t know to what extent they were. He had already come into contact with weapons refining, and for some strange reason, he found a liking for it.
Seeing the chaos during the auction brought back his curiosity.
"I don’t know if you are aware of this, but Soul Spirits aren’t something that can easily be obtained."
"How so?" Kent asked.
"Soul Spirits belong in the underworld."
"Enlighten me."
Lady Wu nodded and began to speak, "I don’t know how deep your knowledge goes, but souls are divided into three parts.
We have the Soul Essence, which almost every soul cultivator can absorb after every kill. It is also what is contained in most soul treasures.
The second is the Reincarnation Soul. This soul enters the cycle of reincarnation, and based on one’s good or bad Karma, they are reincarnated into the next life.
This soul is not even visible to cultivators, regardless of how perceptive they are. Whenever a Spirit beast or human dies, their reincarnation soul enters the cycle of reincarnation.

The last one is the Soul Spirit, which belongs in the underworld. Some say that if the owner of the Soul Spirit possesses good Karma, one day their soul spirits will aid their reincarnated selves in walking the heavenly path
However, unlike the Reincarnation Soul, this one can be seen and can be seized.
However, there is a catch. For one to be able to seize a Soul Spirit, you must be willing to battle the invisible force that binds the Soul Spirits to the channels of the Underworld.
That is something that cannot be achieved easily.

Of course, catching the Soul Spirit of a beast that doesn’t have innate intelligence is considered easy, but when it comes to intelligent beings, aside from a few people, you are the only person I know walking around with two Tier 18 Soul Bodies.
And what is even more shocking is that the one we sold is from a Forsaken Race.
Now, as to why they fought over it—it was because whoever manages to buy it is destined to have a powerful Soul Puppet on their hands once refined."
"Soul Puppets?" Kent raised his brow, hearing a familiar name. Subconsciously, he felt a strong attachment to that name, but his mind was blank of any recollection of where it came from.
In a way, he felt a sense of deja vu.

"Yes, Soul Puppets. They are refined from Soul Spirits. Once refined, not only would they become powerful, but they would also be invulnerable to physical attacks. The only thing that can kill them is soul attacks."
Lady Wu laughed. "And let me tell you, killing a Soul Puppet is next-level impossible."
Kent nodded calmly, unsure of how to handle his next move. If he went ahead and sold one more Soul Spirit, then soon there would be powerful beings walking around this part of the universe.
However, his hesitation was settled when Lady Wu spoke.

"Of course, when it comes to refining soul puppets, the success rate is not great. However, with some luck, even if they don’t get a Tier 18 Soul Puppet out of it, they can surely get a Tier 17, which is enough.
After all, it is a Forsaken Soul Spirit; they can grow without any restrictions or limitations."
"Sounds like a good field of cultivation." Kent stood up, took out the Soul Flag, and waved it. A Tier 18 Soul Spirit from the Forsaken Race appeared, causing the look in Lady Wu’s eyes to shine.
"I will be going around to experience nature, so I might not be around for the Annual Auction. As promised, auction this and take 40% for yourself, and deposit the rest into my account.

Once I return, we will discuss possible business deals for the future. All I ask for is sincerity and honesty. Also, keep my name hidden, and if someone pressures you, tell them my name is Jest, a wanderer."
Lady Wu nodded and stored away the precious Soul Spirit. She took out a communication crystal and handed it over to Kent.
"I will reach out when I come around."
With a wave, Kent left the auction house. A couple of seconds later, he appeared outside and walked toward the guards.
They stood calmly with glints in their eyes as Kent approached.
"I presume you have bank cards," Kent asked, and then nodded. Taking out his card, he swiped it against theirs, and in no time, 100 million Spirit Stones were deposited into their accounts.

"Nice doing business with you two. Until next time." Kent vanished into thin air, but the two guards didn’t even seem to realise. The shock they were in was so much that they didn’t even know when Kent left.

chapters.title: Chapter 936: Time To Become The Faceless Assassin
paragraphs: After leaving the auction house, Kent moved in the direction of a store that sells weapons.
In his mind, whether the lady lived or died was none of his business.
Well, that was his thought at first. However, now he would do everything in his power to protect the lady for two reasons.
First, he planned on obtaining the Soul Puppet Refining Technique from her.
The feeling he got whenever he heard discussions about soul refining was exactly the same feeling he experienced when he first held a sword or lit his first flame.
That excitement was the drive he felt at the moment, compelling him to seek out this Soul Puppet Refining Art for himself.
The dedication on the lady’s face while bidding for the forsaken soul spirit was enough to tell him what he needed to know.
The second reason, of course, was to build future connections.
If he managed to win her trust, which he could by simply saving her sorry ass, then in the future, he would not have to struggle much.
With how much chaos his name is already causing in the future, he knew he must build some connections here now.
So Kent chose to save her, and at that moment, he planned on using his past life as the Faceless Assassin to handle this threat.

So far, he could sense twenty powerful presences in the city, each eyeing the two gates leading in and out of the city. Some were also monitoring the teleportation channels and other modes of travel in and out of the city.
They wanted the soul spirit, and they would do anything in their power to obtain it.

"I don’t know much of Faceless life, but I know enough to get the job done," Kent sighed. "I don’t know what will happen if I were to dive back into my past life memories, so I will make do with what I have now.
After all, I already have the Faceless Art and a few dagger techniques. I also have extensive knowledge when it comes to poison, thanks to my alchemy path, so this should be easy."
An evil smile appeared on Kent’s face. "I doubt Faceless ever had a Soul Map that could look eighty thousand kilometres around him."
After a couple of minutes of walking, Kent arrived at a three-story store that sells only weapons.
"Welcome to Green Bridge Weapons Shop. How can we be of service, handsome?" a lady greeted Kent as soon as he walked in.
Kent, polite and easygoing as ever, smiled and responded, "I am looking to buy some weapons today."
"Oh, do you plan on going hunting?" the lady asked with a smile.
"Something like that." Kent, of course, did not tell her that he indeed planned on going hunting and that his first target was just twelve blocks away.
The lady smiled and said, "What type of weapons do you prefer? We have all kinds of weapons."
"I plan on buying a dagger or two." Kent looked around and added, "I wouldn’t want to stress you, so if you don’t mind, kindly take me to where the top-quality daggers are displayed."
The lady raised her brow at Kent’s words. She studied him for a few moments, unsure whether to take him seriously.
In the end, she shook her head and gestured for him to follow her.
Meanwhile, the other workers around smirked when they saw the lady leading Kent up the stairs.
"If selling a top-shelf item were that simple, do you think any of us would still be here now?"
"What a loser. She thinks just any Core Formation failure that enters the store has what it takes to buy our top-shelf products."
"I know, right? She’s just desperate to make a big sale since she hasn’t sold anything for the past three months."
"Yeah. If she fails to make a sale in the next two days, I’m sure she’ll be sent to one of the smaller stores in the other towns."
While they ridiculed her, she acted as though she hadn’t heard them and led Kent past the second floor until they arrived at the top floor.
Kent was shocked to see only fourteen items there. The lady noticed the look in his eyes and chose to address it.
"This isn’t the main store in this city. If you want the top-tier items, you’ll need to visit the main store, located here in the Central Region. It’s about 60 thousand kilometres from here"
"I see." Kent walked closer to the only dagger on display and picked it up.
"This is the Silver Wolf Dagger. It is a Mystical-grade dagger made from the bone of a Tier 17 Wolf. Special runes have been imbued into it that make it faster when thrown or swung."
Kent looked at the price tag and smiled.
"Just ten million," he muttered, causing the lady to raise her brow.
Of course, he knew ten million here was several times more expensive in a Medium World. However, with the wealth he had accumulated, ten million is mere change for him.
He casually scanned the dagger and placed it back before looking at the other items.

There was a normal bow, a crossbow, a couple of swords, and a gauntlet. The most expensive item there was the gauntlet. Although it was also a Mystical-grade item, its price tag was fifty million spirit stones.
Kent turned and looked at the lady. "What is your name?"
"Veth..." Although she didn’t know why Kent asked for her name, she answered anyway.
Kent smiled. "Well, Veth, today is your lucky day. I’ll be buying all fourteen items here. I hope that will be enough to raise your standing in this humble store."
For a moment, Veth stood frozen, unsure of how to react. When she managed to regain her composure, she looked at Kent with widened eyes.
"Are you being serious?" she asked.

Kent smiled. "Of course I am. I heard how those four spoke ill of you, and while I’m not in the business of saving fairies in distress, you endured all that and still maintained your professionalism, never looking down on me.
So, I’ll reward you. Buying all these items will surely elevate your status."
Veth didn’t say anything. She stood there for a few minutes before suddenly going down on her knees to thank Kent.
"No need for that. You should hurry and complete this sale so you can earn your commission."
Veth stood up, and with a smile suppressing a full-blown laugh, she retrieved a jade crystal and channelled her energy into it.
Three lights—white, blue, and purple—appeared on the crystal. She selected the purple, and then she began scanning the items. In no time, all fourteen items were scanned.
"Altogether will be two hundred and forty million spirit stones. With the discount applied to all fourteen items, you’ll only need to pay one hundred and ninety million."
Kent took out his bank card and tapped it against the crystal in Veth’s hand. One hundred and ninety million was deducted from his account.
"And now for your commission. Take out your own personal bank card," Veth raised her brow with a surprise expression as Kent deposited the remaining fifty million into it.
He waved his hand, and all fourteen items vanished into his space ring.
"On that note, nice doing business with you, Veth." Kent began walking toward the door. Veth followed him, and on the way, she asked for Kent’s name.
The dragon bastard smiled and looked at her. "I am Kent Madson. Be sure never to forget it."
When they reached the ground floor, Kent didn’t even bother to look at the other workers who had badmouthed Veth and left.
After he was gone, Veth retrieved the jade crystal and tapped it against a much larger jade crystal. When it lit up purple, every last jaw dropped.

chapters.title: Chapter 937: Strange Old Man
paragraphs: Veth held the small jade crystal against the larger jade crystal, a smile that came from deep within her soul playing on her lips as she recorded her sale.

The four other sellers in the store opened their jaws wide as they stared at her with envious expressions. Naturally, that envy twisted into shock when purple lights began streaming from the smaller jade into the larger one.
"How?" one of them asked, her expression a mixture of shock, envy, and regret.

Vexthra noticed their expressions first and replied, "How, you ask? It turns out that the handsome Core Formation stage cultivator, whom you all looked down on before he even entered the store, is very rich.
He bought all fourteen Mystical Weapons, and I am recording my sales. So, if you don’t mind, I’d like to finish up here first."
Veth turned back to her business, and a few minutes later, she was done. She picked up a coat, slipped it on, and began walking out of the store.
"Where are you going?" one of them asked.
Veth halted mid-step, turned slowly, and with a teasing smile on her face, she answered,
"Since none of you have ever sold a Mystical-grade item, you don’t know the protocols. However, I will tell you this—I’ve sold fourteen of them.

In this store, if you sell one Mystical-grade item, you are entitled to certain benefits, which include a special commission on the sale. If you sell two, you will be promoted to a much larger store than this one.

But now that I have sold fourteen Mystical-grade items, I might be sent to a different world to oversee all operations at the Green Bridge Weapons Shops in that world. I might even gain the power to hire and fire employees as I please."
A cold light flickered in Veth’s eyes, causing the four women staring at her to turn pale.
Veth laughed and turned away to leave. "So long, losers."
With that remark, she melted into the bustling crowd on the busy street and walked toward the nearest teleportation channel that led to the Central Region.
Ten kilometres away from the store, Kent smiled as he watched and heard everything Veth said.
"She sure knows how to rub salt into their wounds."
He kept the Soul Map open. Although it was rather unpleasant to maintain sight over an eighty-thousand-kilometre radius, he needed to keep his chosen targets within view.
He wanted to cultivate the Faceless Art.
That meant he had to kill, and so far, he had already spotted the right people. Once he eliminated them, he could borrow their faces and act however he pleased in the past.
Naturally, he already had plans to ensure every last target he had marked would fall by midnight. If all goes according to plan, he will complete the mission in a couple of hours, at most.
With that thought, he continued toward a shop he had noticed earlier.
This particular shop specialised in poison herbs.
Kent quickened his steps.
However, as he neared the store, he suddenly felt a sharp gaze lock onto him. The source of that gaze was an old man seated in a lotus posture, with a few ancient books displayed neatly before him.
The gaze was sharp yet not hostile. It was filled with a peculiar, piercing curiosity. That was the only reason Kent had even bothered to pay attention.

On his way here, he had sensed several hostile gazes, which, thanks to the Soul Map, he easily traced back to their sources. Naturally, they were all scum hoping to rob a Core Formation youth like him.
But this old man’s gaze was different. It was sharp, steady, and laced with interest rather than malice.
Kent turned and walked toward him. When the old man saw Kent approaching, he calmly withdrew his gaze and began dusting the covers of the books laid out on the mat.

"I’ve been told I have sharp senses, old man. That was the core reason why I noticed you watching me. Can I ask what this senior wants?" Kent said with a faint smile as he stopped in front of the old man.
The old man lifted the straw hat he wore, revealing a face etched with wisdom and age.

"Truly remarkable. This old man has roamed the universe for thousands of years, and apart from a few others from the powerful Worlds like the sword worlds who sensed my gaze, this is the first time I’ve met someone so young and weak who sensed my gaze.
I cannot help but wonder—could this little one be a swordsman?"

There was nothing to hide, for at that moment Kent sensed no threat from the old man. After all, the elder was only a Spirit King. Even by the standards of a Supreme High World, he posed no threat to Kent.
Or at least that’s what he believed.
"I am indeed a swordsman, currently at the Sword Saint stage," Kent replied calmly.
The old man gave a slow nod, though a fleeting flash of shock crossed his face. He clearly hadn’t expected a mere Sword Saint to detect his gaze.
Kent saw that but said nothing. Instead, he chose to ask a question...
"If you don’t mind me asking, how do the Sword Worlds compare to the Pill Worlds?" Kent inquired.
The old man’s eyes softened, and a faint smile appeared.
"After wandering the Sword Worlds for countless years, I can say with certainty that they are the true havens for cultivators who aim to climb the ladder and become true powerhouses.
Yet, everyone has their own Dao. If one’s Dao lies in the path of Alchemy, then this world is the most fitting place to remain.
But in terms of sheer strength, a true Supreme High World can only be found beyond this star system. This place does not quite reach that standard."
The old man studied Kent’s expression, but found nothing to discern.
With a sigh, he picked up one of the books from the mat before him and handed it to Kent. Then he drew out a jade token from his space ring and gave it to Kent.
"For sensing my gaze, take these two as a reward. This old man can now rest assured that there are still geniuses left in this world.

You must comprehend the book on your own, but the jade token will grant you access to the Serenity of Life and Peace Garden. Should you ever wish to understand the essence of peace, go there—they will guide you."

Kent accepted the items, storing them within his ring. He bowed his head respectfully toward the old man. "Thank you for the gifts. When we meet again, I will be sure to prepare something worthy to offer you in return."
Seeing that the old man had no more words, Kent turned and resumed his journey back toward the shop.
The old man watched Kent’s figure disappear into the crowd, a complex look flashing in his wise eyes.
"So young, yet burdened with such deep hatred and bloodlust." He waved his hand, and the mat and the books before him vanished without a trace.
"I fear it will not be long before a great massacre descends upon this city." He brushed the dust from his robes and stood up, his expression shifting as though some revelation had struck him.
"Time is a complex construct. I once saw it as a vast sea into which anything that steps in sinks. But who would have thought it could also be a blanket that shrouds us?"
Turning once more toward the direction Kent had gone, the old man bowed slightly. "Thank you, little friend. You have helped this old man gain clarity."
With a flick of his sleeve, his figure blurred and vanished into the void, travelling thousands of miles away.
Unaware of the strange encounter that had just taken place, Kent reached the poison herb shop. After a few minutes, he had purchased all the herbs he needed.
Soon, he was ready to begin the hunt.
